papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Objective To examine how the age distribution of radical prostatectomy and radical cystectomy changed in Japan during the period in which robot‐assisted surgery spread. Methods We used the National Database Open Data for fiscal years 2014 to 2024 (Japanese fiscal year, April to March). Procedures were identified by procedure code and classified as robot‐assisted or conventional. Rates per 100,000 population were calculated, and the rate in each age group was expressed relative to that in patients aged 70 to 74 years. Cells with fewer than 10 claims are suppressed in the source tables; sensitivity analyses imputed 0, 5 or 9 procedures into these cells. Results Radical prostatectomy increased from 20,222 to 29,239 procedures and radical cystectomy from 3545 to 4793. Rates in patients younger than 75 years rose only about 1.2‐fold. For prostatectomy, the rate ratio in men aged 75 to 79 years rose from 0.40 to 0.93, while that in men aged 80 to 84 years reached only 0.22. For cystectomy, the ratio in patients aged 80 to 84 years rose from 0.74 to 0.95, while no clear increase was seen in patients aged 85 years or older (0.18 to 0.20, p = 0.791). In men aged 80 years or older, robot‐assisted prostatectomy increased from 94 to 1239 procedures, whereas conventional surgery changed from 64 to 97. These findings were unchanged when suppressed cells were imputed as 5 or 9. Conclusions Between fiscal years 2014 and 2024, the age distribution of radical prostatectomy and radical cystectomy in Japan shifted toward older patients. The increase was concentrated in men aged 75 to 84 years for prostatectomy and in patients aged 80 to 84 years for cystectomy, and was accounted for mainly by robot‐assisted procedures.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Joint modeling (JM) of longitudinal and time‐to‐event (TTE) data is a powerful statistical technique that elucidates how temporal changes in a biomarker relate to TTE outcomes while accounting for study confounders. The growing use of next‐generation sequencing (NGS) in precision oncology, particularly in capturing circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) methylation via liquid biopsy, offers new opportunities to apply JM for patient prognostication. In this study, we used JM to analyze a prospective cohort of 251 non‐small cell lung cancer patients receiving standard‐of‐care immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment regimens. The JM is comprised of two sub‐models—a hierarchical cubic spline random effects model for the longitudinal biomarker component and a Cox proportional hazards model for the TTE outcome component. Each sub‐model incorporated baseline factors of age, gender, smoking status, and cancer stage. The main objective was to establish whether the evolution of a methylation‐derived tumor fraction (TF) is associated with patient outcomes. Our investigation revealed that TF is strongly associated with both real‐world overall survival and real‐world progression‐free survival. These results enable the generation of various patient‐level predictions that capture the dynamic interplay between TF and patient outcomes, offering a path toward real‐time, personalized prognostication. Although validation in larger, multi‐center cohorts is needed before routine adoption, this work represents an important step toward integrating dynamic predictions into serial liquid biopsy monitoring. This approach demonstrates the potential of JM to provide more nuanced and adaptive disease evolution monitoring, offering better clinical decision guidance compared to static models or imaging alone.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction Immune‐related adverse events (irAEs) are complications associated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Hematologic irAEs (heme‐irAEs) are rare but potentially serious and may interfere with cancer treatment. However, their clinical characteristics remain insufficiently described. Methods We conducted a single‐center retrospective study using the National Cancer Center Hospital East medical database from April 1, 2014, to March 31, 2024. Potential heme‐irAE cases were identified using diagnostic name searches, bone marrow examination records, and positive DAT results and were followed by chart review to exclude alternative etiologies, such as chemotherapy‐related myelosuppression, marrow involvement, infection, and hematologic malignancy. Results Of the 3371 patients treated with ICI‐containing regimens, 40 patients developed heme‐irAEs, indicating an observed incidence of 1.2%. The most common heme‐irAE reported was immune thrombocytopenia, and 85.0% of these events were Grade 3 or higher. The median time from ICI initiation to heme‐irAE onset was 12 weeks. For all affected patients included in the regimen‐specific onset‐time comparison, the median time to heme‐irAE onset appeared shorter with dual ICI therapy without chemotherapy than with ICI monotherapy, although this descriptive comparison was based on a small number of cases. ICI‐containing regimens were interrupted or discontinued in most patients, and systemic corticosteroids were administered to 25 patients, 18 of whom achieved hematologic improvement. Cancer treatment was resumed or continued for 20 patients, with no recurrent heme‐irAEs observed during the follow‐up period. In an exploratory landmark analysis, hematologic response was associated with longer survival after heme‐irAE onset. Conclusion Heme‐irAEs were rare but frequently severe in this Japanese single‐center cohort. Their occurrence was associated with prolonged interruption of cancer treatment, underscoring the importance of early recognition, careful diagnostic evaluation, and multidisciplinary management of heme‐irAEs. Our findings regarding dual ICI therapy, survival, and subsequent ICI therapy after heme‐irAE onset should be interpreted as exploratory.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Objective To explore the perioperative changes in inflammatory–immune–nutritional indicators in patients with advanced gallbladder cancer (GBC), defined as American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) Stage III–IV, and to assess whether individual indicators provide incremental prognostic information beyond conventional clinicopathological factors. Methods Patients with pathologically confirmed advanced GBC who underwent surgery at the Department of Hepatobiliary Surgery, National Cancer Center/National Clinical Research Center for Cancer/Cancer Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and Peking Union Medical College, between 2010 and 2022 were retrospectively enrolled. Preoperative and postoperative Day 7 values of the albumin‐to‐alkaline phosphatase ratio (AAPR), albumin‐to‐globulin ratio (AGR), albumin–bilirubin score (ALBI), advanced lung cancer inflammation index (ALI), monocyte‐to‐lymphocyte ratio (MLR), neutrophil‐to‐lymphocyte ratio (NLR), prognostic nutritional index (PNI), and systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) were calculated. Perioperative dynamic changes were compared, and Cox proportional hazards models were constructed to evaluate the incremental prognostic value of these indicators. Results Among 103 patients with advanced GBC, all eight inflammatory–immune–nutritional indicators showed significant changes between the preoperative period and postoperative Day 7. Several preoperative and postoperative indicators were associated with cancer‐specific survival (CSS) in cutoff‐based exploratory analyses. After the incorporation of these indicators into clinicopathological models, most extended models showed varying degrees of improvement in discrimination and goodness of fit. Conclusion In this single‐center cohort, perioperative inflammatory–immune–nutritional indicators exhibit significant dynamic changes in advanced GBC and can improve, to a certain extent, the prognostic performance of models based on conventional clinicopathological characteristics. These indicators may serve as useful supplementary tools for risk stratification and individualized prognostic assessment in patients with advanced GBC.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The diagnostic landscape for the Philadelphia‐negative myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs), particularly in distinguishing Essential Thrombocythemia (ET) from Polycythemia Vera (PV), is compromised. The gold standard for diagnosing PV—measurement of red cell mass (RCM) by radioisotope dilution—has been largely abandoned, leading to widespread misclassification. Thus, an estimated 30%–50% (varying by diagnostic center and testing practice) of JAK2V617F ‐positive ET patients may, in fact, have “hidden” PV, depriving them of the cornerstone PV therapy: phlebotomy. This diagnostic inaccuracy exposes a sizable patient population to an unfortunate high risk of life‐threatening thrombotic events. Concurrently, the management of established PV is suboptimal, often relying solely on hematocrit, a flawed parameter especially in iron‐deficient or hydroxyurea‐treated patients. This perspective calls for the revival and clinical implementation of the Carbon Monoxide (CO)‐rebreathing technique as a promising, rapid, and nonradioactive alternative for RCM assessment. Herein, we review the history of this methodology and discuss its potential to improve MPN care by ensuring precise diagnosis, guiding rational phlebotomy, and ultimately reducing thrombotic morbidity and mortality, while also candidly addressing the current evidentiary and practical limitations that must be resolved before clinical adoption, while also offering potential health‐economic benefits.

papers.abstract: Abstract Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC; age <50 years) has increased in high-income countries. We updated a nationwide Swedish cohort study with data from 2020 to 2024 to compare recent trends with those reported during 1993-2019. Using the National Cancer Register, we identified all incident EOCRC at ages 20-49 years. Temporal trends in age-standardized incidence were assessed using segmented Poisson regression with a breakpoint at 2020 to estimate annual percentage changes (APCs). A total of 1616 EOCRC cases were diagnosed during 2020-2024. Annual percentage changes for left-sided colon and rectal cancers were consistent with continued increases in incidence. In contrast, right-sided colon cancer showed a significant change in trend (P = .01), with a nonsignificant decline during 2020-2024 (APC −3.48, 95% CI = −7.88 to 1.14). These findings indicate that the continued rise in EOCRC is primarily driven by distal tumors, that is, left-sided colon and rectal cancers. Continued surveillance is needed to clarify long-term patterns and underlying drivers.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality among women in Uzbekistan, exceeding WHO elimination targets. Despite a school-based HPV vaccination program launched in 2019, screening coverage remains low, leading to delayed diagnoses; we examined cervical cancer trends in Tashkent (2014-2024) to evaluate the impact of the Korea Foundation for International Healthcare (KOFIH) screening project and UNFPA/UNDP HPV testing initiatives. Methods We analyzed Tashkent City Oncoregister data for women diagnosed with invasive cervical cancer or carcinoma in situ (CIS) between 2014 and 2024 (n = 2140) after data cleaning. We calculated age-standardized incidence and mortality rates, assessed survival using Kaplan-Meier methods, and identified mortality predictors using Cox regression models. Results The age-standardized incidence of invasive cervical cancer was 14.9 per 100 000. After KOFIH and UNFPA/UNDP implementation, CIS diagnoses increased 3.4-fold (0.2-4.7 per 100 000), while the proportion of advanced-stage (III-IV) disease declined by 43%. Five-year survival showed clear stage dependence, ranging from 91.5% for CIS to 27.8% for stage IV. Age and stage were independent predictors of mortality. Crude mortality declined from 10.2 to 1.1 per 100 000 from 2014 to 2024, and case fatality decreased from 48.6% (2014-2019) to 27.2% (2020-2024). Conclusion Organized screening through KOFIH and UNFPA initiatives can improve early detection and reduce mortality. However, 76.6% of staged invasive cases remain advanced (II-IV), and more than 80% of women have never been screened, underscoring the need to expand screening, sustain HPV vaccination, and strengthen prevention programs in Central Asia.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Gastric cancer (GC) has posed a severe threat to human health. Metabolomics analysis has been applied in the context of multiple diseases, offering new perspectives for the development of non‐invasive detections. Objective We aimed to develop a diagnostic model for GC based on a serum bile acid (BA) panel. Methods A total of 632 participants were recruited for serum samples collection, and their clinical characteristics were recorded. Targeted BA profiling was conducted using ultra‐performance liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (UPLC–MS). Participants from Xi'an were randomly allocated into a training cohort and an internal tuning cohort at a 7:3 ratio. The key BAs were identified through the two‐step selection method, and nine machine learning (ML) models were constructed and optimized. The optimal model was further evaluated externally using an independent validation cohort from Lanzhou. Results A panel of 10 serum BAs was confirmed for the construction of a diagnostic model. The XGBoost model exhibited the best performance on the tuning cohort, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.858. It also exhibited robust performance on the external validation cohort (AUROC = 0.816), significantly outperforming tumor markers (with the highest AUROC of CA72‐4 = 0.68). The developed model also demonstrated satisfactory predictive performance for patients with resectable stage GC (Stage I–II) (average precision [AP] = 0.75). Conclusion GC patients exhibit BA metabolic disorders. The XGBoost model based on a 10‐BA panel exhibited superior efficacy in GC detection, indicating its promising potential for clinical application.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Estrogen receptor (ER)‐positive/HER2‐positive breast cancer demonstrates significantly lower rates of pathological complete response (pCR) to neoadjuvant HER2‐targeted therapies compared to ER‐negative/HER2‐positive disease. However, the optimal ER positivity cutoff for clinically meaningful patient stratification remains undefined. Methods We analyzed a retrospective cohort of 741 HER2‐positive breast cancer patients treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy plus dual HER2 blockade (trastuzumab and pertuzumab) at Sun Yat‐sen University Cancer Center. The optimal ER cutoff for predicting pCR was determined by ROC analysis with Youden index and validated by bootstrap resampling (1000 iterations). Transcriptomic data from TCGA and SCAN‐B cohorts were analyzed to characterize biological differences between ER subgroups. Drug response was predicted using the oncoPredict algorithm, and cancer dependency was assessed using DepMap CRISPR screening data. Results ER ≥ 50% positivity was identified as the optimal predictive cutoff (bootstrap 95% CI: 25.0%–77.5%) and was an independent predictor of significantly lower pCR rates in multivariate analysis (OR = 0.27; 95% CI: 0.19–0.40; p < 0.001). Transcriptomic analysis revealed that ER ≥ 50% tumors are characterized by activated estrogen response signaling, downregulated cell cycle and immune pathways. Predicted resistance to trastuzumab, T‐DM1, and T‐DXd was consistently enriched in this subgroup, consistent with lower HER2 and CD16A expression observed in ER ≥ 50% tumors. CCND1, a canonical transcriptional target of ESR1, was significantly upregulated in ER ≥ 50% tumors across both cohorts, and ER + /HER2 + cell lines exhibited significantly higher CCND1 and CDK4 dependency scores in DepMap CRISPR screening ( p < 0.05), supporting activation of the ESR1‐CCND1‐CDK4/6 axis in this subgroup. Conclusions ER ≥ 50% positivity defines a clinically and biologically distinct HER2‐positive subgroup with poor response to standard neoadjuvant therapy and predicted resistance to ADCs, consistent with lower HER2 and CD16A expression in this subgroup. The convergent transcriptomic and functional evidence for ESR1‐CCND1 axis activation provides mechanistic support for combining CDK4/6 inhibitors with endocrine and anti‐HER2 therapies to improve outcomes in this resistant subgroup.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Cyclin E1 (CCNE1), a pivotal member of the cyclin family, governs the G1/S phase transition of the cell cycle by binding to and activating cyclin‐dependent kinase 2 (CDK2), thereby initiating DNA replication and driving S‐phase entry. In a broad spectrum of human malignancies—including breast, ovarian, gastric, and non‐small cell lung cancers—amplification or overexpression of CCNE1 disrupts the orderly regulation of cell cycle progression, leading to uncontrolled proliferation, impaired DNA damage repair, and genomic instability. These oncogenic consequences are intimately associated with increased tumor aggressiveness, poor patient prognosis, and diminished therapeutic efficacy. This review provides an integrated examination of CCNE1 biology, spanning its physiological regulation in the cell cycle, the molecular mechanisms by which its dysregulation drives tumorigenesis and drug resistance, the clinical implications of CCNE1 amplification as both a prognostic biomarker and a predictor of therapeutic response, and the emerging strategies to target CCNE1‐driven vulnerabilities. By synthesizing findings across diverse cancer types and regulatory layers, we evaluate the translational potential of CCNE1 as a diagnostic marker and therapeutic target, and highlight key challenges and opportunities for future investigation.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Non‐pathological complete response (non‐pCR) is common in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) patients after neoadjuvant therapy, yet evidence guiding long‐term outcomes and postoperative risk stratification in the immunotherapy era remains limited. Methods We retrospectively enrolled consecutive ESCC patients treated with neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy (nICT) or chemotherapy alone (nCT) followed by esophagectomy and restricted analyses to non‐pCR cases. Primary endpoints were five‐year overall survival (OS) and event‐free survival (EFS). A 1:1 optimal propensity score matching (PSM) procedure and administrative censoring at 60 months were applied. Survival outcomes were assessed using Kaplan–Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses. Results Among 366 patients with non‐pCR disease, 164 matched pairs were generated. After matching, nICT demonstrated a higher major pathological response (MPR) rate (19.5% vs. 6.1%), a lower ypT4 proportion (3.7% vs. 22.0%), and fewer recurrence/metastasis rate (40.2% vs. 58.5%), all p < 0.001. In the matched multivariable Cox model, nICT was independently associated with a lower risk of EFS events (HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.36–0.84; p = 0.005), whereas no independent association with OS was observed (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.70–1.27; p = 0.707). Open esophagectomy (OE), ypN2‐3 disease, and perineural invasion (PNI) were associated with worse EFS, whereas lower Ki‐67 expression and postoperative adjuvant treatment were associated with better EFS. PNI was associated with worse OS, and postoperative adjuvant treatment was associated with better OS. Conclusion Among non‐pCR ESCC patients after neoadjuvant therapy and surgery, nICT was associated with lower recurrence risk and improved five‐year EFS compared with nCT, whereas a significant OS advantage was not observed. Pathological factors (PNI, high Ki‐67, and residual nodal burden) and postoperative treatment may help inform risk stratification, although the observational treatment associations should be interpreted cautiously.

papers.abstract: Abstract Epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) drives immunotherapy resistance in lung cancer through three interconnected axes: antigen/checkpoint dysregulation, chemokine remodeling, and metabolic reprogramming. We highlight partial EMT (pEMT) as a clinically prevalent hybrid state and biomarker candidate, and metabolic rewiring as an actionable immunometabolic vulnerability. EMT signatures may complement programmed death receptor ligand-1 (PD‑L1), but require treatment-by-biomarker interaction testing. Integrating these axes enables resistance-subtype stratification and precision combination therapy.

papers.abstract: Abstract Despite the availability of various treatment modalities for liver cancer, its mortality rate remains high. Immunotherapy represents an emerging approach for liver cancer. However, the response rate to single-agent immune checkpoint blockade therapy is suboptimal. Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) oxidoreductase 1-alpha (ERO1A), a potential therapeutic target associated with ER stress, is implicated in impeding protective antitumor immunity. In this study, we found that targeting ERO1A in liver cancer while activating the protein kinase R-like ER kinase/eukaryotic initiation factor 2 alpha subunit/activating transcription factor 4/C/EBP homologous protein–mediated apoptosis and autophagy signaling downregulated adenosine A1 receptor and inhibited the cyclic guanosine monophosphate–protein kinase G pathway, thereby promoting the expression and secretion of C-C chemokine ligand 4. This led to an increased infiltration of CD8+ T cells into the immune microenvironment, enhancing the antitumor immune response. Furthermore, targeting ERO1A in liver cancer also upregulated type I interferon synthesis, activated the Janus kinase–signal transducers and activators of transcription pathway, and promoted programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1) and MHC-I expression. Using liver cancer animal models, we demonstrated that combination treatment with an ERO1A inhibitor and a PD-L1 inhibitor increased CD8+ T-cell infiltration and enhanced their function within the tumor microenvironment, resulting in synergistic antitumor effects. Therefore, ERO1A represents a promising therapeutic target in liver cancer, potentially suitable for combination with immune checkpoint inhibitors to improve patient outcomes.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction Cancer care is burdensome, but patient experience with time and administrative burdens is variable. Our objective was to assess the association between daily administrative tasks, time spent, and reported burden and identify demographic and clinical predictors. Methods Participants ( n = 122) from two longitudinal studies of individuals receiving cancer treatment utilized a mobile application (Daynamica) to track time spent on cancer care tasks over 28 days. Participants reported distress levels (NCCN Distress Thermometer) and time spent on three administrative tasks daily: scheduling appointments, managing medical bills/claims, and arranging support/transportation. Relationships between distress and tasks were assessed using generalized linear mixed models. Results Most participants (91.8%) performed at least one administrative task during the study. Participants were more likely to report clinically significant distress (score 4+) on days involving administrative tasks (scheduling [OR = 1.92, 95% CI: 1.40–2.64], managing bills [OR = 2.10, 95% CI: 1.34–3.29], or arranging support [OR = 3.56, 95% CI: 2.19–5.79]) compared to days without these tasks. While the median time spent was low (14 min per week; Q1–Q3: 3–39), the top quartile spent an average of 83 min per week on these tasks. Lack of reliable transportation was the only factor significantly associated with increased time spent on administrative tasks (median 57 vs. 10 min/week, p = 0.01); no other demographic or clinical factors were associated with higher workload. Conclusion Administrative burden is a distinct psychological stressor for individuals with cancer, regardless of the actual time required for administrative tasks. Interventions should focus on streamlining insurance, care coordination, and administrative processes to reduce patient distress. papers.abstract: Abstract Background In acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), minimal residual disease (MRD) is an established biomarker of treatment response and strongly associated with poor outcomes. Among children with ALL, air pollution has been associated with lower survival but has not been evaluated with prognostic biomarkers like end of induction (EOI) MRD. Methods Using the Reducing Ethnic Disparities in Acute Leukemia (REDIAL) Consortium, we analyzed 2,125 pediatric patients with ALL. Daily fine particulate matter (PM2.5) estimates were obtained from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and linked to patients’ residential and treatment center census tracts. Mean daily PM2.5 during induction was calculated using two definitions: 1) based solely on patients’ residential address, and 2) Days 1-7 based on the treatment center and Days 8 to EOI on patients’ residence. Patients were categorized in quartiles based on mean daily PM2.5. EOI MRD ≥0.1% or ≥ 0.01% was considered positive. Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using logistic regression. Results In B-ALL, mean daily residential PM2.5 during induction was associated with positive EOI MRD in quartiles 2 (aOR: 1.56, 95% CI: 1.08, 2.24) and 3 (aOR: 1.51, 95% CI: 1.05, 2.17) but not quartile 4 (aOR: 1.19). The association across all three quartiles strengthened when restricted to NCI high-risk B-ALL (aOR range: 1.73-2.28). Conclusions Residential PM2.5 was associated with positive EOI MRD in patients with NCI high-risk B-ALL. Our findings contribute to a growing body of evidence that environmental exposures are associated with inferior outcomes among children diagnosed with ALL.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Endometrial carcinoma (EC) is one of the most common gynecological malignancies. Aberrant DNA methylation (DNAm) is an important epigenetic alteration involved in cancer progression. Long non‐coding RNAs (LncRNAs) play critical roles in gene regulation and pathological processes. However, the biological and prognostic significance of lncRNA‐mRNA pairs associated with methylation remains unclear. Methods Transcriptomic, DNA methylation, and clinical data from The Cancer Genome Atlas were integrated to construct a differentially methylated sites (DMSs)‐lncRNA‐mRNA network. After mapping DMSs to their corresponding differentially methylated genes (DMGs), the DMS‐mediated network was further represented as a DMG‐lncRNA‐mRNA tripartite network. After removal of DMG nodes, a DMG‐associated lncRNA‐mRNA background network was constructed, and key lncRNA‐mRNA pairs were prioritized according to their topological importance using weighted shortest‐path calculation and PageRank‐based random walk algorithms. The methylation‐associated lncRNA‐ mRNA pair (MLMP) model was then established based on univariate Cox, LASSO Cox, and multivariate Cox regression analyses. Results Eight DMG‐associated lncRNA‐mRNA pairs were selected to construct the MLMP model. Under a common analysis framework, the MLMP model achieved higher area under the curve (AUC) values than 17 previously published prognostic signatures for overall survival prediction. Patients in the low‐MLMP group had significantly better overall survival than those in the high‐MLMP group. Functional enrichment and immune microenvironment analyses indicated that the MLMP model was associated with immune‐related pathways and distinct tumor immune microenvironment characteristics. Predictive analyses suggested that patients in the low‐MLMP group exhibited higher predicted responsiveness to CTLA‐4/PD‐1 blockade and differential predicted sensitivity to several therapeutic agents. Conclusions The MLMP model may serve as a potential tool for prognostic stratification in EC and provide insights into methylation‐associated lncRNA‐mRNA interactions. The predicted associations with immunotherapy response and therapeutic sensitivity may generate hypotheses for future treatment‐related studies. These findings require further validation in independent clinical cohorts and experimental studies before clinical application.

papers.abstract: Patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remain at high risk of relapse despite perioperative treatment1-3. NeoCOAST-2 (NCT05061550), a phase 2, randomised platform trial, tested novel perioperative treatments in patients with stage IIA-IIIB NSCLC. At primary analysis, combining standard chemotherapy plus durvalumab (anti-PD-L1 antibody) with oleclumab (Arm 1, n = 76), monalizumab (Arm 2, n = 72) or datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd; Arm 4, n = 54) resulted in pathological complete response (pCR) rates of 20.3%, 25.7%, and 35.2%, respectively4. Here, we present the first report of prespecified secondary endpoints of event-free survival (EFS) and circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) clearance, and exploratory analyses of associations between ctDNA dynamics and clinical outcomes. The 24-month EFS rates were 70.5%, 75.7% and 77.9% in Arms 1, 2 and 4, respectively. Using a tumour-agnostic assay, ctDNA clearance at neoadjuvant Cycle 3 Day 1 was highest in Arm 4 (50.9%, 54.5%, and 72.5% in each arm, respectively). ctDNA clearance correlated with prolonged EFS versus non-clearance (pooled hazard ratio (HR) 0.22; 95% CI = 0.11-0.45, P = 0.0000443). Patients with both ctDNA clearance and pCR had favourable EFS outcomes versus those with neither (EFS HR 0.10, 95% CI = 0.02-0.42, P = 0.002). These findings suggest combined assessment of ctDNA clearance and pCR may improve risk stratification, and that the numerically highest pCR4 and EFS rates with the Dato-DXd combination warrant further evaluation.

papers.abstract: Although nonpharmacological interventions are recommended for preventing perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND), cognitive training has not been explicitly advocated. Therefore, this systematic review and meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis (TSA) and meta-regression tested the hypothesis that preoperative cognitive training, compared with usual care, reduces the incidence of PND. Eight databases and two clinical trial registries were searched for RCTs comparing preoperative cognitive training with usual care. Primary outcomes were postoperative delirium (POD), delayed neurocognitive recovery (DNR), and postoperative neurocognitive disorder. Thirteen RCTs with 1446 patients were identified. Preoperative cognitive training was associated with a lower risk of POD (RR 0.53; 95% CI 0.36-0.77; P = 0.001; low certainty). Subgroup analysis (P for interaction = 0.01) and meta-regression (β1 1.072, 95% CI 0.006-2.138, P = 0.049) suggested an association between training format and treatment effect on POD, with a potentially greater benefit for traditional training. For DNR, the incidence was lower in the training group than in the usual care group (RR 0.66; 95% CI 0.46-0.96; P = 0.03; very low certainty), but this finding was not supported by several sensitivity analyses. No significant differences were detected between subgroups for training format, total duration, or surgery type (P for interaction = 0.06, 0.37, and 0.34, respectively), and meta-regression suggested that overall risk of bias was a potential moderator for DNR (P = 0.045). TSA suggested a potential for false-positive findings, as the cumulative Z-curves did not cross the TSA boundaries, and the required information sizes were not reached for either outcome. Preoperative cognitive training may reduce the incidence of POD, with traditional training showing a potentially greater benefit than digital training. For DNR, the current evidence is insufficient to support a preventive effect of preoperative cognitive training, although a trend toward benefit was observed. These findings are limited by high risk of bias in several included trials and failure to reach the required information sizes in TSA, particularly for DNR, which need to be confirmed in future large-scale RCTs. papers.abstract: To our knowledge, UNION is the first phase 3 trial to assess a neoadjuvant strategy incorporating radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and chemotherapy compared with standard care in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, which reported positive results for the primary endpoint (blinded independent review committee [BIRC]-assessed pathological complete response rate; 39·8% vs 15·3%). Here, we present a prespecified interim analysis of event-free survival. This open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial was conducted at nine hospitals in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years with untreated cT3-4 or N+ rectal adenocarcinoma (≤10 cm distance from the anal verge) and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1; stratified by clinical T stage and N stage), using permuted blocks, to receive neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions) followed by two cycles of intravenous camrelizumab (200 mg on day 1) plus CAPOX (oral capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1-14 and intravenous oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 on day 1; experimental group) or long-course chemoradiotherapy (50·4 Gy in 28 fractions with concurrent oral capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily) followed by two cycles of CAPOX (standard-of-care group). After surgery, both groups received six cycles of adjuvant CAPOX, and the experimental group additionally received adjuvant camrelizumab for up to 15 cycles. The primary endpoint was BIRC-assessed pathological complete response rate in the intention-to-treat population, which has been previously reported. Here, we performed a prespecified interim analysis of investigator-assessed event-free survival (one of the key secondary endpoints, defined as time from randomisation to radiographic progression precluding surgery, local recurrence or distant metastasis, or death) in the intention-to-treat population (all randomly assigned patients) with a boundary of a two-sided p values less than 0·0102. Safety was evaluated in all patients who received at least one dose of the study treatment according to the assigned regimen. The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04928807, and is active, but no longer recruiting. Between July 23, 2021, and March 1, 2023, 231 patients (153 [66%] males and 78 [34%] females; 227 [98%] were Han Chinese, and four [2%] were other ethnicity Chinese) were randomly assigned to the experimental group (n=113) and standard-of-care group (n=118). As of Oct 1, 2025, the median follow-up duration was 36·7 months (IQR 32·6-39·9) in the experimental group and 34·7 months (31·1-39·1) in the standard-of-care group. The 3-year investigator-assessed event-free survival rate was 91·3% (95% CI 83·9-95·4) in the experimental group versus 77·4% (67·9-84·4) in the standard-of-care group (stratified hazard ratio 0·33 [0·15-0·71]; two-sided log-rank p=0·0029). During the entire treatment period, the most common grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were decreased lymphocyte count (23 [20%] of 115 in the experimental group vs 31 [28%] of 112 in the standard-of-care group), decreased white blood cell count (13 [11%] vs 16 [14%]), decreased neutrophil count (13 [11%] vs 13 [12%]), and decreased platelet count (seven [6%] vs 15 [13%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 22 (19%) versus 15 (13%) patients, with the most common being decreased platelet count (one [1%] vs six [5%]), and radiation gastroenteritis (two [2%] vs four [4%]). Treatment-related deaths occurred in one patient in the experimental group (septic shock related to chemotherapy, but unrelated to camrelizumab) and none in the standard-of-care group. In this interim analysis, short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and CAPOX significantly improved 3-year event-free survival in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, with a safety profile similar to long-course chemoradiotherapy followed by CAPOX. Comparison of this promising new treatment strategy with contemporary total neoadjuvant therapy strategies is warranted. papers.abstract: Abstract Regulatory T (T reg ) cells in mice can lose lineage identity and acquire proinflammatory functions, but whether human T reg cells are similarly susceptible to cytokine-driven destabilization remains unclear. Here we established an in vitro model of human T reg cell destabilization defined by silencing of the lineage-specifying transcription factor FOXP3, loss of suppressive function and acquisition of proinflammatory activity. Single-cell chromatin accessibility and transcriptomic profiling revealed a genome-wide increase in accessibility at AP-1-binding sites, including a putative regulatory element distal to IRF4 . Increased accessibility at this element correlated with increased IRF4 expression during T reg cell destabilization, and its excision conferred resistance to inflammatory cytokine-induced reprogramming. Conversely, forced expression of IRF4 together with BATF promoted T reg cell destabilization. These data identify a distal IRF4 regulatory element as a critical node enabling heightened AP-1-IRF4 cooperative activity to drive T reg cell destabilization, with implications for the design of more stable and effective T reg cell-based therapies.

papers.abstract: Abstract Sickle cell disease (SCD) is an inherited hemoglobinopathy characterized by chronic hemolytic anemia, painful vaso-occlusive episodes, and end-organ damage. Cellular therapies, including allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT) and gene therapy, are potentially curative treatments for SCD. Cases of myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukemia (MDS/AML) occurring after cellular therapy for SCD and reports of an increased relative risk of AML in populations with SCD have raised questions about the association between SCD and clonal hematopoiesis (CH), a recognized precursor state for MDS/AML. We used error-corrected DNA sequencing to detect CH variants at a variant allele fraction >0.0005 in blood samples from 98 individuals with SCD and 72 donor controls without SCD who underwent HCT at the National Institutes of Health or an outside hospital (n = 2) between July 2004 and June 2023. Baseline CH prevalence was similar in recipients and donors; however, recipients with SCD had 3.8-fold higher odds of DNA damage response (DDR)–mutant CH involving TP53, PPM1D, ATM, and CHEK2 compared with donors without SCD. After HCT, the proportion of recipients with SCD with CH increased, driven primarily by mutations in DNMT3A/TET2 and TP53. Post-HCT CH arose from newly emergent variants undetectable at baseline in both recipient and paired donor samples, engrafted donor-derived CH, and persistent recipient CH. All cases of donor-derived CH involved DNMT3A/TET2 mutations, whereas persistent recipient CH involved DDR mutations. Hematologic neoplasms were rare but included 3 cases of fatal TP53-mutant MDS/AML. Larger cohort studies are needed to identify the risk factors for developing DDR-CH and MDS/AML in SCD and to optimize cellular therapy safety in this population.

papers.abstract: Background Engineered bacterial therapeutics represent a promising strategy for sustained intestinal delivery of therapeutic molecules, but their efficacy is limited by inefficient colonisation, safety concerns and the need for repeated administration or auxiliary delivery systems. Objective To develop a safety-optimised native bacterial chassis capable of long-term gut colonisation and sustained therapeutic delivery for intestinal inflammatory and metabolic diseases. Design Native murine Escherichia coli isolates were screened for antibiotic susceptibility, genetic tractability and long-term intestinal colonisation. The selected strain, MEc30, was further optimised by deleting the putative virulence-associated clb and irp loci. MEc30 was then engineered to produce nicotinic acid (MEc30-NA) or deliver murine interleukin-10 (MEc30-mIL-10), and therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in a high-fat diet-induced metabolic dysfunction model as well as Il10 −/− and dextran sulphate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis models. Results MEc30 achieved stable lifelong colonisation of the murine intestine after a single oral administration, without antibiotic preconditioning or auxiliary delivery systems and did not detectably disturb host physiology or gut microbial ecology. Deletion of clb and irp abolished potential colibactin- and yersiniabactin-associated biosafety risks while preserving bacterial growth and colonisation capacity. MEc30-NA continuously produced nicotinic acid in the gut, activated epithelial GPR109a-associated barrier signalling, improved glucose and lipid metabolism, reduced systemic inflammation and avoided the sharp peak exposure associated with conventional nicotinic acid administration. MEc30-mIL-10 enabled sustained intestinal interleukin-10 delivery, suppressed inflammatory macrophage activation, improved barrier integrity and alleviated colitis in both Il10 − / − and DSS-induced mouse models. Conclusion This study identifies MEc30 as a durable and safety-optimised native E. coli chassis for sustained intestinal therapeutic delivery. Engineered native symbionts may provide a long-acting live biotherapeutic strategy for metabolic diseases and chronic intestinal inflammation.

papers.abstract: Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (Atezo-Bev) is a standard first-line systemic therapy for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). We aimed to explore the benefits of adding curative locoregional therapy (LRT) to patients who achieve a partial response (PR) to Atezo-Bev treatment. This multinational retrospective study enrolled patients who received Atezo-Bev as first-line systemic therapy for unresectable HCC and reached complete response (CR) or PR. Patients were categorized into three cohorts: patients who underwent curative LRT after PR, patients with PR but did not receive curative LRT, and patients achieving CR without LRT. Curative LRT included surgery, ablation, and definitive radiotherapy with imaging evidence showing disease-free status afterward. A total of 243 patients were enrolled from 8 countries or regions; 31 patients received curative LRT after PR, 180 patients obtained PR but did not receive curative LRT, and 32 patients achieved CR without LRT. The curative-LRT group, compared with patients who did not receive curative LRT after PR, exhibited significantly longer PFS (median, 44.4 months vs. 18.2 months, p = 0.004) and overall survival (OS) (median, not reached vs. 34.3 months, p < 0.001). The differences remained significant after inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) adjustment. By contrast, whether before or after IPTW adjustment, the curative-LRT group did not exhibit statistically significant difference in PFS, OS, and recurrence-free survival from patients who obtained CR without curative LRT. Curative LRT may consolidate the efficacy of Atezo-Bev in patients achieving a PR, potentially prolonging survival compared to systemic therapy alone.

papers.abstract: Early progressive disease (early PD) at the first imaging assessment during atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (Atezo/Bev) therapy may represent primary resistance and is associated with poor outcomes in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC). This study aimed to quantify the frequency, prognostic impact, and baseline predictors of early PD in a large real-world cohort. Consecutive patients with uHCC who initiated Atezo/Bev therapy at 28 institutions in Japan (September 2020-August 2025) were retrospectively analyzed. Early PD was defined as PD at the first on-treatment imaging assessment, according to the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1. Overall survival (OS) was compared using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Baseline predictors were examined using prespecified multivariable logistic regression with multiple imputation: the primary multivariable model included Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) stage C and alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) ≥400 ng/mL, while an alternative tumor-feature model including extrahepatic spread (EHS) and macrovascular invasion (MVI) was evaluated as a sensitivity analysis. Among 685 treated patients, 666 were evaluable at the first imaging assessment, of whom 148 (22.2%) had early PD. The median OS was 333 days in the early-PD group versus 768 days in the non-early-PD group (log-rank p < 0.001). In the primary multivariable model, AFP ≥ 400 ng/mL (OR 2.33, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.58-3.43) and BCLC-C (OR 1.76, 95% CI: 1.15-2.68) independently predicted early PD. In the alternative tumor-feature model, AFP ≥ 400 ng/mL (OR 2.50, 95% CI: 1.69-3.69) and EHS (OR 1.52, 95% CI: 1.03-2.23) remained significant predictors, whereas MVI did not. Two-point baseline scores (AFP ≥ 400 plus BCLC-C or EHS) stratified the risk of early PD in a stepwise manner, reaching approximately 40% in the highest-risk group (p for trend < 0.001). Early PD occurs in approximately one-fifth of patients with uHCC treated with Atezo/Bev and is associated with markedly poorer OS. AFP ≥ 400 ng/mL and BCLC-C provide a pragmatic baseline risk stratification approach that may help guide early monitoring and treatment sequencing.

papers.abstract: Vessel encapsulating tumor cluster (VETC) defines a distinct vascular phenotype of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), characterized by tumor nests fully encased within a continuous endothelial lining. This architecture correlates with poor prognosis and enhanced sensitivity to anti-angiogenic therapies. To dissect the morphological, phenotypical, molecular, and functional programs that define VETC-associated ECs in HCC and to identify endothelial pathways potentially driving VETC vascular organization and tumor progression. Biological samples (blood, plasma, Peripheral blood mononuclear cells, and tissue) were collected from VETC+ and VETC- HCCs. Quantitative tissue imaging was integrated with EC-specific molecular profiling. Vascular architecture was assessed on whole-slide images, and purified tumor ECs underwent targeted and transcriptome-wide gene expression analyses. ECs from both VETC+ and VETC- HCCs lacked pro-growth and anti-apoptotic features. VETC+ ECs show overexpression of pro-angiogenic and immune-modulatory factors, in particular vascular endothelial growth factor alpha, FGF and IL10, and a specific gene signature involved in metabolic reprogramming, increased trafficking and migratory capacity. VETC+ transcriptional phenotype is driven by a coordinated hepatic xenobiotic-sensing network in which HNF4A and HNF1A provide the dominant regulatory architecture, while NFE2L2 contributes a distinct regulatory layer governing the antioxidant response elements-dependent arm of the xenobiotic and oxidative-stress response. VETC+ ECs actively shape the HCC microenvironment through the release of angiogenic and immunomodulatory cues. These findings support the existence of a specialized angiocrine program in VETC+ HCC.

papers.abstract: Radiological response dynamics may provide prognostic information beyond conventional response categories in patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) receiving atezolizumab plus bevacizumab. Building upon findings from the IMbrave150 trial, we evaluated the prognostic significance of depth of response (DpR), duration of response (DoR), and time to response (TTR) in a real-world cohort. This retrospective multicenter study included 183 treatment-naïve patients with unresectable HCC treated with atezolizumab plus bevacizumab between November 2020 and September 2024. Tumor response was assessed according to mRECIST. Associations of DpR, DoR, and TTR with overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were evaluated using landmark analyses and time-dependent Cox analyses. Deeper tumor response, longer DoR, and ≥50% reductions in serologic biomarker correlated with improved survival. Patients who achieved an early response (≤2 months) tended to have less favorable survival outcomes than those with a later response. Multivariate analysis confirmed DoR (HR = 0.40; 95% CI: 0.30-0.55; p < 0.001) and DpR (HR = 0.45; 95% CI: 0.38-0.55; p < 0.001) as independent predictors for improved OS, while early response independently predicted worse OS (HR = 1.64; 95% CI: 1.26-2.15; p < 0.001). Similar trends were observed for PFS. Exploratory analyses suggested a potential association between conversion surgery and prolonged OS. DpR and DoR were independently associated with survival outcomes in patients with unresectable HCC receiving atezolizumab plus bevacizumab, extending and validating previous findings from IMbrave150 in a real-world setting. The prognostic significance of TTR and conversion surgery warrants further prospective investigation.

papers.abstract: Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (Atezo/Bev) has been recommended globally for patients with Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) stage C hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); however, this regimen has shown modest survival benefits. Therefore, this study aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of Atezo/Bev with or without transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) as first-line treatment for BCLC C HCC. This nationwide multicenter retrospective cohort study recruited patients with BCLC stage C HCC from 14 medical centres who received TACE combined with Atezo/Bev (TACE+Atezo/Bev) or Atezo/Bev alone as first-line treatment between October 2020 and January 2025. To mitigate potential confounding imbalances between groups, propensity score matching (PSM) and stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (sIPTW) were applied. Overall survival (OS) was set as the primary endpoint, with progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (ORR), and safety assessed as the secondary endpoints. Of the 256 patients included in the analysis, 154 received TACE+Atezo/Bev and 102 received Atezo/Bev. After PSM, analysis of 96 patients per group showed that the TACE+Atezo/Bev group significantly extended the median OS (25.9 months vs. 15.2 months, p < 0.001) and PFS (15.8 months vs. 7.4 months, p < 0.001), compared with the Atezo/Bev group. Post-application of sIPTW, 154 patients were assigned to the TACE+Atezo/Bev group and 102 to the Atezo/Bev group, and the median OS (25.3 vs. 15.4 months, p < 0.001) and PFS (15.5 vs. 7.5 months, p < 0.001) were significantly longer in the TACE+Atezo/Bev group than in the Atezo/Bev group. A higher ORR was observed in the TACE+Atezo/Bev group compared with the Atezo/Bev group (primary cohort: 48.7% vs. 31.4%, p = 0.009; PSM cohort: 51.0% vs. 31.2%, p = 0.008; sIPTW cohort: 50.6% vs. 32.0%, p = 0.005). Moreover, Grade 3/4 adverse events (AEs) occurred in 60 patients (39.0%) in the TACE+Atezo/Bev group and 34 patients (33.3%) in the Atezo/Bev group. Compared with Atezo/Bev alone, TACE+Atezo/Bev may significantly improve ORR, PFS, and OS as first-line treatment for BCLC stage C HCC, while maintaining an acceptable safety profile.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Early delayed gastric conduit emptying (DGCE) and pneumonia are among the most common complications following oesophagectomy. These issues can be challenging to address during minimally invasive surgery with pyloroplasty or pyloromyotomy. This study evaluated the impact of prophylactic endoscopic pyloric balloon dilatation (PBD) on early postoperative outcomes. Methods Consecutive patients undergoing oesophagectomy with gastric conduit reconstruction for cancer at two Australian tertiary centres (2017–2025) were retrospectively analysed. From 2023, intraoperative endoscopic-assisted PBD using a 20 mm balloon inflated for two minutes across the pylorus was adopted as standard practice. Primary endpoints were early DGCE and hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) within 30 days; secondary endpoints included nasogastric tube (NGT) output and duration, and hospital length-of-stay. Associations were examined using multivariable logistic regression and inverse-probability-weighted regression adjustment (IPWRA). Results Of 187 patients, 40 (21.4%) received PBD. Compared with controls, PBD was associated with reduced DGCE (15% vs. 40.1%; odds ratio [OR] 0.26, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.11–0.65) and HAP (20% vs. 40.8%; OR 0.36, 95% CI 0.17–0.80). Pyloric balloon dilatation independently predicted lower DGCE (OR 0.33, 95% CI 0.12–0.91) and HAP (OR 0.18, 95% CI 0.05–0.67), with absolute risk reductions of 27.4% and 30.8% respectively on IPWRA analysis. Pyloric balloon dilatation was also associated with lower postoperative NGT outputs, earlier NGT removal (median 6 [interquartile range (IQR) 4-11] vs. 4 [IQR 3–7] days; p = 0.032), and shorter hospital length of stay (median 13 [IQR 9–22] vs. 9 [IQR 8–16] days; p = 0.007). Conclusions Prophylactic PBD was associated with lower early DGCE and pneumonia. This enabled earlier nasogastric tube removal and shorter hospital stay, supporting its integration into contemporary practice.

papers.abstract: Long-term head and neck cancer survivors are few, but always exposed to a risk of mandibular osteoradionecrosis (ORN) despite the use of appropriate dose-volume constraints in today's radiotherapy. Here, ORN development is approached from another look, in an attempt to explain its complexity. Early ORN is best defined by length of the mucosal defect (<2 teeth long) and radiological assessment of the depth of areas of bone resorption (lysis below the level of the inferior alveolar canal) in the radiotherapy volume. Technical improvements have greatly reduced the incidence of ORN, but a lifelong risk remains and requires long-term follow-up. Pathogenic hypotheses have evolved over time from the "radiation-trauma-infection" triad to the 3H theory of "hypoxia-hypocellularity-hypovascularity", and then radiation-induced fibro-atrophy of the bone. ORN is a dynamic process combining interacting causal factors that worsen each other over time: (a) radiation-induced fibro-atrophy of the bone and its related radiotherapy technical parameters; (b) periodontal disease/dental trauma and their related questions on optimal timing of pre- or post-radiotherapy extractions and how many teeth; (c) infection/oral microbiota and their related mechanically inaccessible bone sequestra (residual bacteria); (d) vascular factors from capillary network destruction to artery stenosis of irradiated branches and the carotid trunk. Symptomatic medical care focusing on comorbidity parameters and devitalized tissue removal is not sufficient to protect patients against ORN. These new insights should help to treat early ORN through concomitant control of these causal factors and best dental care.

papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly expanding across gynecologic oncology, but most applications remain focused on image interpretation and retrospective prediction rather than direct support of treatment decisions. This review examines how AI is progressing from imaging biomarkers toward multimodal decision-support systems that integrate radiologic, pathologic, molecular, and clinical information. We summarize current applications in ovarian, endometrial, and cervical cancers, with particular attention to preoperative risk stratification, surgical planning, radiotherapy, systemic treatment selection, treatment-response prediction, and multidisciplinary decision-making. Multimodal approaches are especially promising because they reflect the way clinical decisions are made and may provide greater value than models based on a single data source. However, the current evidence remains dominated by retrospective and often single-center studies, with limited external and prospective validation. Data heterogeneity, domain shift, incomplete multimodal datasets, bias, workflow integration, regulatory requirements, and model monitoring remain important barriers to routine implementation. We therefore outline a stepwise pathway for clinical translation, from robust multicenter validation and prospective human-AI evaluation to clinical-impact studies and post-deployment monitoring. The next phase of AI in gynecologic oncology should prioritize clinically meaningful decisions and measurable patient or workflow benefit rather than incremental gains in predictive performance alone.

papers.abstract: Background Steatohepatitic hepatocellular carcinoma (SH-HCC) is a distinct subtype of hepatocellular carcinoma with poorly defined molecular features and limited diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. Objective This study aimed to delineate its multi-omics landscape, develop non-invasive diagnostic tools and identify actionable therapeutic targets. Design We integrated multimodal clinical and omics datasets from an overall cohort of 156 patients, including RNA-seq (n=69), spatial transcriptomics (n=36), spatial metabolomics (n=6), lipidomics (n=125) and serum proteomics (n=152), for comprehensive molecular profiling and diagnostic model construction. FABP4 was functionally validated in Sleeping Beauty-induced HCC mouse models. Results An SH-HCC index was established to reliably differentiate SH-HCC from conventional HCC. Drug response analysis suggested a potential reduction in responsiveness to sorafenib and immunotherapy-based regimens in SH-HCC, whereas transarterial chemoembolisation may remain an effective therapeutic option. Spatial transcriptomics revealed increased immune cell infiltration, a reinforced immune barrier and reduced tumour-immune cell communication. SH-HCC is characterised by a lipid-rich phenotype, and a diagnostic model based on 12 lipid species showed good performance in an independent cohort (area under the curve (AUC)=0.909). Serum proteomic model demonstrated good performance in the test cohort (AUC=0.828). Importantly, our preliminary findings suggest a potential therapeutic role for FABP4, as its genetic deletion suppressed tumour growth, reshaped the tumour immune microenvironment and enhanced the response to PD-1 blockade. Conclusion This study provides the first multi-omics characterisation of SH-HCC, highlighting the SH-HCC index and non-invasive diagnostic models, with FABP4 as a potential target.

papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is often diagnosed after the opportunity for curative treatment has passed. Blood-based biomarkers offer opportunities for earlier detection and serial molecular assessment, but their value depends on the intended clinical use. This nonsystematic narrative review critically examines circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), circulating tumor cells, extracellular vesicles, circulating RNAs, proteins and multimodal panels, including models developed using artificial intelligence. We distinguish population screening, high-risk surveillance, diagnostic evaluation, molecular profiling, treatment monitoring and postoperative recurrence assessment. High discrimination in selected case-control cohorts does not establish performance in asymptomatic populations or clinical benefit. Differences in disease stage, comparator groups, sample handling and validation design preclude reliable ranking of biomarker classes using published area-under-the-curve values. ctDNA has a more established role in selected molecular-profiling situations than in early detection; postoperative detection and longitudinal changes provide prognostic information, but do not by themselves justify treatment modification. Multimodal assays require comparison with clinical assessment and CA19-9 at prespecified thresholds, external validation, calibration and evaluation of downstream harms and costs. This review presents an intended-use framework and a summary of representative prospective studies. Limitations include purposive, non-exhaustive evidence selection and the absence of formal risk-of-bias or certainty grading. Clinical translation requires reproducible assays and evidence that biomarker-informed decisions improve outcomes. Liquid biopsy should therefore be evaluated within defined clinical pathways alongside imaging, pathology and established molecular testing.

papers.abstract: Cisplatin has been a standard chemotherapeutic agent for advanced non-small cell lung cancer for decades. Conventionally administered intravenously, it undergoes systemic distribution, exposing both tumour and healthy tissues to the drug. Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle injection of cisplatin is emerging as a potential intratumoural drug delivery (ITDD) strategy. However, rigorous preclinical research is needed before ITDD can be more widely adopted. We used our experimentally induced ovine pulmonary adenocarcinoma (OPA) model, generated by Jaagsiekte sheep retrovirus (JSRV) infection, to evaluate transthoracic and transbronchial ITDD techniques. We compared systemic platinum exposure following intravenous cisplatin delivery with that following intratumoural cisplatin administration. Both non-recovery and recovery studies were conducted in a total of eight sheep. ITDD techniques were successfully developed and performed in three tumour bearing sheep during non-recovery procedures. To provide a reference for systemic platinum exposure, intravenous cisplatin was administered to three JSRV-infected sheep that did not develop OPA. Intravenous administration produced a rapid plasma platinum peak followed by a rapid decline. ITDD resulted in preferential platinum deposition within targeted lung tumours while producing substantially lower systemic platinum exposure compared with intravenous administration. Intratumoural cisplatin delivery was also evaluated in a recovery procedure using a single sheep, comparing single-site and fractionated administration over a 28-day period, with tumour biopsies confirming lesion presence before treatment. Following ITDD, tumour volumes were observed to decrease over the study period. The recovery experiments demonstrated the feasibility of repeated tumour biopsies, intratumoural injections, longitudinal CT monitoring and recovery anaesthesia using the OPA model. To our knowledge, this is the first report of direct intratumoural cisplatin administration into ovine lung tumours. This study also provides proof-of-concept that this clinically relevant large animal lung cancer model can serve as a translational platform for evaluating intratumoural therapeutic delivery strategies relevant to human lung cancer.

papers.abstract: To identify latent psychological resilience profiles in older patients after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) and examine their association with physical resilience. A total of 300 patients with prostate cancer were recruited from a Class III Grade A hospital in Sichuan Province between December 2025 and May 2026. Assessments were conducted on postoperative day 3 using the general information questionnaire, Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale, and Physical Resilience Instrument for Older Adults. Latent profile analysis was performed using the total score on the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale. Generalized linear regression was used to analyze the relationship between psychological and physical resilience across categories among elderly patients after RARP. Three latent psychological resilience profiles were identified among older patients after RARP. Physical resilience scores differed among people with different psychological resilience. The results of generalized regression analysis showed that patients in different psychological resilience profiles of RARP patients were related to their physical resilience (P < 0.05). Older patients after RARP showed heterogeneous psychological resilience profiles, and profile membership was associated with physical resilience. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to determine the temporal direction and clinical utility of these profiles.

papers.abstract: Advanced recurrent gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) after prolonged tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) exposure requires integration of surgical oncology, molecular reassessment, and continuous systemic therapy. We report a 72-year-old man with a 21-year history of gastric GIST who underwent initial resection in 2005, resection of recurrent disease in 2009, and long-term imatinib therapy. After years of apparent disease stability, he independently reduced imatinib and had a prolonged surveillance gap before recurrence was detected in 2024. Following tumor rupture and short-interval progression on sunitinib and regorafenib, he received ripretinib. In January 2026, clinically necessary maximal cytoreductive surgery was performed for bulky recurrent peritoneal disease with bleeding, anemia, abdominal-wall involvement, high risk of re-rupture, and invasion or close involvement of the right colon. Pathology confirmed recurrent high-risk spindle-cell GIST. Postoperative next-generation sequencing identified a founding KIT exon 11 deletion and a secondary KIT exon 17 p.Asn822Tyr activation-loop mutation; ripretinib was resumed after recovery of oral intake. Three-month CT showed recurrent peritoneal tumors, while a right hepatic subcapsular low-enhancement nodule was favored to represent post-ablation change. This case illustrates that surgery in resistant recurrent GIST may be necessary for local complication control and tissue acquisition, but even after maximal macroscopic cytoreduction, durable management depends on continuous genotype-informed systemic therapy and close surveillance.

papers.abstract: Urothelial carcinoma is a common urinary malignancy with high incidence, recurrence, and mortality. Early diagnosis is pivotal for improving patient outcomes. Current standards have important limitations: cystoscopy, although the cornerstone of diagnosis and surveillance, is invasive and costly, while cytology has limited sensitivity for low-grade or early-stage lesions. Urine, as a liquid biopsy, offers a non-invasive and repeatable approach for sampling urogenital pathology, with the potential for longitudinal monitoring through serial collection. The review covers urinary multi-omics biomarkers, including cfDNA/methylation, miRNAs, extracellular vesicles (EVs), and proteomic/metabolomic signatures. We summarize their performance in early detection, staging, and postoperative monitoring. Integrated multi-analyte models, including true multi-omics assays and multiplex single-omics panels, generally outperform single biomarkers, with some panels achieving >90% sensitivity and >95% specificity in prospective cohorts. Despite progress, several challenges remain: standardization, large-scale prospective validation, and regulatory/reimbursement barriers. We conclude that urinary multi-omics diagnostics are promising complementary tools that may optimize surveillance and risk stratification. Still, limited prospective validation, lack of standardization, and the persistent risk of false-negative results constrain adoption. On current evidence, they are not positioned to replace cystoscopy, which remains the cornerstone of diagnosis and surveillance, particularly in non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC). However, their most realistic and immediate clinical role is as a triage tool to optimize the selective use of cystoscopy-particularly for risk-stratifying patients with hematuria, adjudicating equivocal cytology, and potentially reducing the frequency of invasive surveillance in low-risk NMIBC patients.

papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide and frequently arises in the setting of chronic liver disease, cirrhosis, and portal hypertension. Liver resection represents a cornerstone of curative-intent treatment, but its role is uniquely influenced by the need to balance oncologic radicality with preservation of functional liver parenchyma. Over the last two decades, minimally invasive liver surgery has progressively expanded from selected laparoscopic minor resections to complex laparoscopic and robotic hepatectomies, challenging the historical dominance of open surgery. This narrative review critically examines the evolving roles of open, laparoscopic, and robotic liver resection for hepatocellular carcinoma, emphasizing patient selection, technical considerations, scenario-based platform choice, and comparative outcomes. Particular attention is given to hepatocellular carcinoma-specific challenges, including impaired liver function, clinically significant portal hypertension, future liver remnant adequacy, recurrence risk, and the need for parenchymal-sparing strategies. The review also discusses distinct clinical scenarios, including small solitary tumors, posterosuperior lesions, central or deeply located tumors, multifocal disease, and recurrent HCC. Current evidence consistently suggests that minimally invasive approaches are associated with reduced blood loss, fewer postoperative complications, and shorter hospital stay compared with open surgery, while maintaining comparable oncologic outcomes in selected patients. Laparoscopy remains the most established minimally invasive platform, whereas robotics may offer technical advantages in complex resections through improved dexterity, three-dimensional visualization, and enhanced suturing capability. However, available evidence remains largely retrospective and influenced by selection bias and institutional expertise. Platform selection should therefore be individualized according to tumor anatomy, liver function, technical complexity, and center experience, with the goal of maximizing oncologic benefit while minimizing functional liver loss.

papers.abstract: Treatment of relapsed refractory follicular lymphoma (R/R FL) still remains challenging. Several strategies have been used against R/R FL. Recently, two chemotherapy-free regimens have gained space, epcoritamab-lenalidomide-rituximab (Epco-R2) and tafasitamab-lenalidomide-rituximab (Tafa-R2). Herein, we performed an indirect trial comparison (ITC) between the two regimens using the Bucher method as they both have the common comparator arm R2. The ITC between the two study arms showed an overall response rate (ORR; p = 0.020), and complete remission rates (CR; p < 0.0001), in favor of Epco-R2. Analysis regarding time to next treatment (TTNT) interval also favored Epco-R2 (p = 0.0011). The ITC in the progression free survival (PFS) context showed the anchored comparison favored Epco-R2 over Tafa-R2 [HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.31-0.86)], p = 0.011, a finding more pronounced in patients with progression of disease within 24 months (POD24) negativity. Regarding the safety profile, Epco-R2 was associated with more hematological toxicity and infections, whereas, Tafa-R2 was associated with more COVID-19 infections probably reflecting the pandemic era enrollment timing. In conclusion, Epco-R2 is more effective in terms of treatment outcomes, but comes with greater toxicity. Tafa-R2 seems more suitable for patients with limited bone marrow reserves, patients who wish to avoid hospitalization, patients at a higher risk for cytokine release syndrome, and patients with high-risk infection vulnerability. Finally, this is not a direct comparison of two therapeutic regimens and the results should be cautiously interpreted. Treatment choice should be decided on a case-by-case scenario based on several different variables.

papers.abstract: Although combining systemic and locoregional therapies has improved outcomes for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), identifying appropriate candidates remains challenging because no reliable tool predicts response. This retrospective multicenter study enrolled 334 HCC patients who received first-line locoregional-systemic therapy from nine centers in China. Following automated tumor segmentation using nnU-Net on pretreatment contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging, predefined radiomics features were computationally extracted, and deep learning features were obtained via a ResNet convolutional neural network. Three types of predictive models for tumor response (radiomics, deep learning, and combined) were developed and validated on the training cohort (n = 213), internal validation cohort (IVC, n = 53), and external validation cohort (EVC, n = 68). Performance was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and net reclassification improvement (NRI). Associations of model with progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were evaluated. Among the three models (multi-sequence radiomics, multi-sequence deep learning, and combined), the combined model showed the best predictive performance in both the training (AUC: 0.997, 95% CI: 0.994-1.000) and validation cohorts (AUC of IVC 0.900, 95% CI: 0.806-0.994; AUC of EVC: 0.871, 95% CI: 0.790-0.951). The combined model demonstrated significantly improved predictive performance compared with the multi-sequence radiomic model (training NRI = 43.9%, p < 0.001; IVC NRI = 38.7%, p = 0.038; EVC NRI = 3.2%, p = 0.806) and multi-sequence deep learning model (training NRI = 80.8%, IVC NRI = 72.7%, EVC NRI = 50.4%; all p < 0.05). Specifically, the combined model was significantly associated with both PFS and OS. The combined radiomics-deep learning model outperformed both single-modality models in predicting objective response and stratifying survival outcomes in unresectable HCC patients receiving combined systemic and locoregional therapy.

papers.abstract: People with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) often have underlying comorbidities, which may impact prognosis and lead to safety challenges following treatment. This exploratory, post hoc analysis of the phase 3 HIMALAYA study (NCT03298451) assessed outcomes in participants with unresectable HCC and cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities at baseline. Participants with unresectable HCC were randomized to STRIDE (Single Tremelimumab Regular Interval Durvalumab), durvalumab monotherapy, or sorafenib. Comorbidities were based on medical history assessed at baseline and qualified using preferred terms from cardiovascular or metabolic Standardised Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities Queries. Overall survival (OS) rates were evaluated in participants with or without cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities within and by treatment group. The proportion of long-term survivors (alive ≥36 months post-randomization) and safety were assessed in participants with cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities. Data cutoffs: August 27, 2021 (primary analysis); January 23, 2023 (4-year updated analysis, OS, and serious treatment-related adverse events). Hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus were the most common cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidities, respectively. The 48-month OS rates with STRIDE were 28.0% and 21.7% in participants with and without cardiovascular comorbidities and 20.4% and 28.5% in those with and without metabolic comorbidities, respectively. In total, 28.2% of participants with cardiovascular comorbidities and 22.6% of participants with metabolic comorbidities experienced long-term survival with STRIDE. Safety in participants with cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities was generally consistent with all participants in the safety analysis set; no new safety signals were observed. OS benefits with STRIDE were similar in participants with vs. without cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities, with manageable safety in participants with comorbidities. These results support the durable benefits of STRIDE in a broad population reflective of unresectable HCC globally.

papers.abstract: The use of evidence in clinical practice is essential for the provision of best practice care in psychosocial oncology. However, research demonstrates gaps in the implementation of evidence-based interventions and important resource barriers for clinicians. Clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) are designed to translate the latest evidence into recommendations applicable within various clinical domains. A recent study identified 23 English-language, up-to-date psychosocial oncology CPGs. The present study sought to systematically assess the quality of these tools. CPGs were independently evaluated by four trained appraisers using the AGREE II tool, consisting of 23 items across six domains. Quality was determined using aggregate and consensus domain scores (0%-100%), with an acceptability cut-off score of 60%. Findings revealed that 20 of the 23 CPGs (87%) met the acceptability threshold (M = 76.45, SD = 12.35). The highest average domain scores were observed for Clarity of Presentation (M = 96.26, SD = 6.25) and Scope and Purpose (M = 87.38, SD = 19.55) while Applicability received the lowest score (M = 33.83, SD = 10.72). Rigor of Development scores (M = 71.17, SD = 17.46) demonstrated substantial variations across CPGs. Findings indicate that psychosocial oncology CPGs are specific and clear but may benefit from more transparency in reporting procedures and greater consideration of applicability and implementation strategies. These findings may help illuminate guideline developers on gaps in current tools and serve to inform clinicians on the strengths and shortcomings of these tools prior to selecting which ones to integrate within their clinical practice.

papers.abstract: University students with cancer in Italy face major barriers in maintaining their academic pathways despite existing disability legislation. This brief communication combines an overview of the Italian legal and institutional context with findings from a community-led qualitative descriptive needs-assessment. Following a national social media call, the analysis included semi-structured interviews with 69 eligible participants. Interviews were documented through contemporaneous written notes and analyzed manually using descriptive content analysis, combining domains from the interview guide with recurrent categories identified in open-ended responses. Participants described administrative burdens, inconsistent recognition of cancer-related needs, limited access to remote learning and flexible examinations, marked variability in university support, emotional distress, and social isolation. These findings provide preliminary real-world evidence of how existing arrangements are experienced by Italian university students affected by cancer. Although specific interventions were not evaluated, the findings may inform the development and prospective assessment of more consistent academic accommodations, accessible information, individualized support, and integrated psychosocial services.
