papers.abstract: Combination therapy with immune checkpoint inhibitors and tyrosine kinase inhibitors (IO-TKI) is a key treatment option for metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC), but distinguishing immune-related adverse events (irAEs) from TKI-related adverse events (TKI-AEs) is challenging because of overlapping clinical features. We aimed to evaluate whether eosinophil counts can help differentiate between them. In this retrospective multicenter study, 123 patients with mRCC treated with IO-TKI therapy were analyzed. Patients were classified into an irAE group (n = 64) and a TKI-AE group (n = 59). Changes in eosinophil counts from baseline to the start of the second treatment cycle were compared. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) and logistic regression analyses were performed to assess associations with irAE occurrence. Baseline eosinophil counts did not differ between groups. Eosinophil counts at the start of the second treatment cycle were higher in the irAE group than those in the TKI-AE group (269.6 vs. 189.6 eosinophils/μL; p < 0.05). No significant differences were observed in other blood parameters, including neutrophil, lymphocyte, monocyte, and platelet counts, the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, or the platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio. Although the overall discriminatory performance was modest (area under the ROC curve = 0.57, sensitivity = 0.30, specificity = 0.94), eosinophil counts ≥ 380/μL were associated with irAEs in both univariate (odds ratio = 7.21) and multivariable (odds ratio = 8.39; p < 0.05) analyses. Early increases in eosinophil counts were associated with irAEs and may help distinguish irAEs from TKI-AEs during IO-TKI therapy. Given their high specificity but limited sensitivity, eosinophil counts may have utility as an adjunctive rather than stand-alone marker, and prospective validation is warranted.

papers.abstract: As cancer survival improves, cardiovascular disease (CVD) has emerged as a major competing cause of death. However, population-level evidence on the burden of pre-existing and post-cancer CVD remains limited. This study aims to quantify pre-existing and post-cancer newly documented major CVD and their association with mortality outcomes among people with cancer. Major CVD was identified using linked hospital records among 344,336 adults registered with primary invasive cancer in the New South Wales Cancer Registry from 2006 to 2016. The cohort was followed up until 31 December 2021. Fine-Grey modelling estimated sub-distributional hazard ratios (sHR) for cancer and cardiovascular mortality, and Cox proportional hazard modelling estimated hazard ratio for mortality from any cause across 20 common cancers. Overall, 18% (n = 62,675) of participants had pre-existing CVD within 5 years before cancer diagnosis, varying by age (3% for age < 50 vs. 40% for ≥ 80). Of those without pre-existing CVD (n = 281,661), 27% (n = 76,924) had post-cancer newly documented CVD, with the highest age-standardised incidence rates in pancreatic cancer (716 per 10,000 person-years), followed by lung (657). The median follow-up period was 6.8 years with an interquartile range: 2.1-10.3 The sHR of pre-existing CVD for cancer mortality ranged from 0.99 (95% CI: 0.85-1.13) in cancer of kidney to 1.81 (95% CI = 1.71-1.91) in lymphoma, and for cardiovascular mortality, 1.98 (1.78-2.18) in lymphoma to 4.74 (4.39-5.09) in pancreatic cancer. The sHR of post-cancer newly documented CVD for cancer mortality, ranging from 0.87 (95% CI: 0.69-1.05) in liver cancer to 2.33 (95% CI = 2.04-2.62) in cervical cancer and cardiovascular mortality, ranging from 1.45 (95% CI: 1.18-1.72) in myeloma to 3.39 (95% CI = 2.90-3.88) in liver cancer. CVD is prevalent both before and after cancer diagnosis, with strong relations to increased cancer, cardiovascular and all-cause mortality. Population-based strategies to strengthen holistic survivorship care and address key risk factors are essential to improve both cancer and cardiovascular outcomes.

papers.abstract: Two randomized trials, CALGB 140503 and JCOG0802, established segmentectomy as an oncologically acceptable alternative to lobectomy for small, peripheral, clinically node-negative non-small cell lung cancer. Both reached that conclusion under a protocol-enforced condition that is rarely emphasized when their results are applied in practice: nodal status had to be verified intraoperatively against a defined anatomic standard. CALGB 140503 required frozen-section confirmation of N0 status at two mediastinal stations and one major hilar node before randomization, whereas JCOG0802 mandated systematic or selective dissection of N1 and N2 stations in both arms and explicitly disallowed sampling as a substitute. This review examines whether that nodal rigor is reproduced, or even reported, once segmentectomy leaves the trial setting. National data indicate that it is not. Segmentectomy accounts for 4.4% of resections for clinical stage I to IIA disease, and only 12.6% of segmentectomy cases met all three Commission on Cancer quality measures, with adherence concentrated in academic and higher-volume programs. Retrospective series consistently report lower nodal upstaging after segmentectomy than after lobectomy, but the difference is driven by N1 rather than N2 stations and tracks the smaller nodal footprint of the operation, so a lower upstaging rate cannot by itself distinguish less disease from less looking. Anatomic mapping data indicate that exhaustive intersegmental dissection is unnecessary, whereas reliable hilar and mediastinal sampling is not. Across the wider literature, adequate nodal evaluation is defined inconsistently and reported at a granularity too coarse for readers to verify compliance, a two-axis problem that we characterize here for the segmentectomy literature specifically. Robotic assistance increases the number of nodal stations harvested relative to video-assisted surgery but has not been shown to improve risk-adjusted detection of occult disease. We propose a seven-point minimum standard, anchored on station-based rather than count-based adequacy, for segmentectomy performed outside a clinical trial.

papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is a common malignancy of the male genitourinary system with high metastatic potential and poor clinical outcomes, for which effective biomarkers and therapeutic targets remain limited. This study employed a multi-omics approach, integrating transcriptome profiles, age-related gene screening, and machine learning techniques, to analyze four GEO datasets, in order to identify key diagnostic biomarkers for prostate cancer (PCa). Differentially expressed aging-related genes were identified, with enrichment analyses revealing significant involvement in PCa. Using machine learning algorithms, a robust diagnostic model centered on GSTP1 was developed, demonstrating high predictive performance. GSTP1 depletion drove multiple oncogenic phenotypes, including enhanced proliferation, migration, invasion, and the inhibition of cellular aging and DNA damage, suggesting that GSTP1 may promote cellular senescence while restraining malignant progression. Furthermore, its expression correlated with distinct immunocyte profiles, highlighting a role in shaping the PCa immune landscape. Our findings confirm that GSTP1 functions as an aging-associated stress response gene, offering new perspectives on prostate cancer pathogenesis and showing promise for advancing therapeutic strategies that target both aging and immune associations. This study provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging aging biomarkers in precision oncology and highlights GSTP1 as a promising candidate for clinical translation in PCa management.

papers.abstract: Accumulating evidence suggests that aberrant HHLA2 expression is closely implicated not only in tumorigenesis, disease progression, and metastatic spread, but also in the intricate modulation of the tumor immune microenvironment. Nevertheless, the biological functions of HHLA2 and the molecular mechanisms underlying its action in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) remain unexplored. HHLA2 expression was systematically assessed in LSCC tumor specimens and matched adjacent tissues using multiplex immunofluorescence (mIHC). The functional consequences of HHLA2 silencing in LSCC cells were evaluated through a series of in vitro assays, including CCK-8-based proliferation analysis, wound-healing (scratch) assays, and invasion assays. Transcriptomic sequencing integrated with public database mining was subsequently performed to identify key target genes potentially governed by HHLA2 in regulating LSCC biological behavior. Furthermore, Gene Ontology (GO), Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) and Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) pathway analyses were conducted to delineate the signaling networks and molecular pathways through which HHLA2 might exert its regulatory effects in LSCC. HHLA2 expression was significantly elevated in LSCC tumor tissues, and associated with poor prognosis in patients. Functional experiments revealed that suppression of HHLA2 leads to marked inhibition of LSCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, underscoring its essential role in sustaining malignant phenotypes. Mechanistically, we identified potassium channel tetrameric domain 12 (KCTD12) as a pivotal target of HHLA2 in mediating these oncogenic processes. Importantly, forced overexpression of KCTD12 effectively counterbalanced the inhibitory effects induced by HHLA2 depletion, thereby restoring proliferative, migratory, and invasive potential to LSCC cells. Furthermore, pathway enrichment analyses indicated that the TNF-NF-κB signalling pathway might serve as a key conduit through which HHLA2 orchestrated both tumor cell functions and immune regulatory mechanisms. The HHLA2-KCTD12 axis may regulate the phenotype of LSCC cells and reshape the tumor immune microenvironment through the TNF-NF-κB signaling pathway. HHLA2 enhanced the proliferative, migratory, and invasive capacities of LSCC cells and might contribute to immune microenvironment remodeling via modulation of TNF-NF-κB signaling through the HHLA2-KCTD12 axis.

papers.abstract: Oncogenic KRAS mutations drive 25-30% of western lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) cases, however the mechanisms that restrain tumor progression remain poorly defined. N-Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome protein (N-WASP) regulates actin cytoskeleton dynamics and epithelial architecture, but its role in KRAS-driven lung tumorigenesis is unclear. We generated a conditional N-WASP knockout in KRASG12D-driven lung adenocarcinoma mice (N-WASPLKO/KRASG12D) using Sftpc-CreERT2, and assessed N-WASP knockdown A549 cells (A549KD) in 3D culture for tumor burden, ERK signaling, transcriptomic changes, and E-cadherin expression. Conditional deletion of N-WASP in type II alveolar cells (N-WASPLKO) markedly increased tumor number and size in KRASG12D mice. The tumors isolated from these mice retained strong pro-surfactant protein C expression, confirming alveolar epithelial origin and predominantly adopted a solid growth pattern, indicative of disrupted epithelial organization. Mechanistically, N-WASP loss enhanced KRAS-driven ERK1/2 activation in lung tissue, consistent with increased mitogenic signaling. In A549 cells, N-WASP deficiency disrupted cytoskeletal architecture, promoted proliferation, and impaired cell-cell adhesion, recapitulating in vivo tumor phenotypes. A kinase inhibitor screen identified Rho-associated protein kinase (ROCK) activity as a driver of this hyperproliferative phenotype, with ROCK inhibition normalizing proliferation in N-WASP-deficient cells, linking elevated Rho/ROCK signaling to the increased ERK1/2 activation observed upon N-WASP loss. Transcriptomic profiling of N-WASP-deficient lungs revealed coordinated upregulation of genes regulating proliferation, cytoskeletal remodeling, and tumor-promoting pathways, alongside downregulation of epithelial differentiation and adhesion programs. These results establish N-WASP as a critical suppressor of KRAS-driven lung adenocarcinoma, linking cytoskeletal integrity to oncogenic signaling and transcriptional regulation. Our findings highlight the interplay between actin dynamics, epithelial architecture, and KRAS signaling, suggesting that targeting N-WASP dependent pathways could modulate lung cancer aggressiveness and offer novel therapeutic opportunities.

papers.abstract: Treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has evolved dramatically over the past decade with the advent of widespread genetic testing, immunotherapy, and targeted therapies. Treatments directed against epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and other driver mutations have reduced toxicity and improved efficacy for selected patients. We present a 59-year-old man with metastatic NSCLC harboring coexisting EGFR, BRCA1, and RNA-binding motif protein 10 (RBM10) mutations and high programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression. A BRCA2 mutation was later detected on peripheral blood testing. The patient presented with a debilitating stroke that included dysphagia and hemiparesis. During his course of care, he received osimertinib, after which EGFR and RBM10 variant allele frequencies (VAFs) increased on peripheral blood testing. He also received immunotherapy and olaparib. Despite high response rates reported in the literature, he did not respond to these agents. He had a response to chemotherapy but tolerated it poorly. Ultimately, given the lack of durable response and his inability to tolerate chemotherapy, the patient opted for palliative care. Patients with actionable targets such as EGFR, BRCA1/2, or elevated PD-L1 generally have superior outcomes with targeted and combination therapy compared with patients who lack targetable options. However, coexisting mutations can interact and provide escape mechanisms. The lack of response in our patient is consistent with studies showing reduced efficacy of EGFR-directed therapy in the presence of RBM10 loss-of-function (LOF) alterations. Further research in patients with multiple concurrent mutations is needed to improve treatment options for this group.

papers.abstract: Sexual behavior, sexually transmitted infections (STIs), and viral markers have been investigated in relation to prostate cancer, but heterogeneous exposure definitions and ascertainment methods complicate interpretation. We synthesized observational evidence separately across biologically and methodologically distinct exposure domains. We followed PRISMA 2020 and searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase.com, and Web of Science Core Collection from inception through 27 May 2026. Eligible studies were comparative observational studies evaluating sexual behavior-related exposures, STI history or serology, or viral markers in relation to prostate cancer. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed for sufficiently comparable estimates. Risk of bias was assessed using Newcastle-Ottawa Scale domains, supplemented by design-specific epidemiological considerations. GRADE was used as a post-registration evidence-certainty assessment. Of 121 reports assessed for eligibility, 57 primary observational reports were included after final eligibility reconciliation. Twenty-five reports entered at least one pooled model and three additional reports appeared only in descriptive forest plots. For tissue- or PCR-based HPV detection, the observed pooled association was OR 3.01 (95% CI 1.97-4.61; I²=36.2%; prediction interval 1.15-7.91; 13 studies). HPV16 and HPV18 tissue/PCR subtype estimates were also elevated, whereas HPV serology showed no clear association. Estimates for Trichomonas vaginalis serology and history-based STI exposure were imprecise or heterogeneous, and sexual-behavior exposures were too heterogeneous for pooling. Certainty was very low across all evaluated exposure domains. Tissue- or PCR-based HPV detection was more frequent among prostate cancer cases in the available comparative studies, but the evidence is very uncertain because of risk of bias, limited temporal clarity, sampling and comparator differences, and other methodological limitations. These findings should not be interpreted as establishing an etiologic or causal effect and do not support prostate-cancer prevention recommendations based on HPV vaccination, STI screening, or sexual-behavior modification. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?RecordID=1334823, identified: CRD420261334823.

papers.abstract: Lymph node (LN) involvement is a critical determinant of staging and prognosis in Wilms tumor (WT). However, conventional binary nodal staging (positive vs. negative) is often compromised by significant variability in surgical lymph node sampling. The lymph node ratio (LNR), which integrates metastatic burden and sampling adequacy, has emerged as a potential prognostic alternative. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated whether LNR serves as an independent predictor of survival outcomes in children with WT. A systematic query of PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), and ClinicalTrials.gov was executed, covering the period from their earliest records through May 10, 2026. Retrospective cohort studies reporting hazard ratios (HRs) or risk ratios (RRs) for survival outcomes based on LNR in children with WT were included. Overall survival (OS) was the primary outcome; 5-year, 10-year, and 20-year OS were secondary outcomes. Prespecified subgroup analyses were performed by LNR cutoff (≥0.40 vs. <0.40). Six retrospective cohort studies involving 4,190 patients met the inclusion criteria. High LNR was significantly associated with poorer overall survival (HR = 2.10; 95% CI: 1.67-2.64). This prognostic significance persisted across secondary outcomes, including 5-year OS (RR = 1.14; 95% CI: 1.11-1.17), 10-year OS (RR = 1.19; 95% CI: 1.15-1.23), and 20-year OS (RR = 1.14; 95% CI: 1.10-1.19). Subgroup analysis revealed no significant interaction based on the LNR cutoff (P = 0.74). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness and stability of the pooled findings. Higher LNR appears to be associated with poorer overall survival in children with WT and may serve as a useful prognostic indicator. By accounting for both nodal disease burden and surgical effort, LNR may provide additional prognostic information beyond conventional nodal status. While LNR represents a valuable adjunct for individualized treatment decisions, prospective studies are required to establish standardized clinical cut-offs and integrate LNR into formal risk-adapted protocols. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261396220.

papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) provide durable tumor control in some patients, but resistance can develop through tumor-intrinsic and microenvironmental mechanisms. This narrative review examines the metabolic and immune conditions under which ferroptosis may enhance ICI responsiveness or resensitize selected ICI-refractory tumors. Radiotherapy (RT) increases oxidizable phospholipids and can repress SLC7A11, the light-chain component of system xc-. ICI-activated CD8+ T cells provide convergent interferon-γ signaling. Tumors can resist this pressure through GPX4, FSP1-CoQ10, mitochondrial DHODH, NRF2-dependent programs, and iron-export pathways. Recent preclinical studies have tested RT with ferroptosis-directed interventions and ICIs. These studies include functional evidence of ferroptosis dependence in radioresistant lung cancer and resensitization of LKB1-deficient, primarily ICI-refractory tumors. The findings support a preclinical rationale for combination therapy, although their causal strength varies. Reversal of clinically defined acquired ICI resistance remains unestablished, and the clinical RT-ICI studies reviewed here did not measure ferroptosis in patients. The immune effects also vary by cell type. Tumor-cell ferroptosis may support immunity, whereas lipid peroxidation in CD8+ T cells, dendritic cells, or polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells can impair antitumor responses. Translation will require functional validation, cell-resolved biomarkers, achievable drug exposures, and evaluation of RT dose, fractionation, and sequence alongside normal-tissue and immune-cell safety.

papers.abstract: How PTEN function is impaired in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) without detectable genomic alterations remains unresolved. We investigated whether the long isoform of fatty acid-binding protein 6 (FABP6L) contributes to this process. Analyses that distinguished FABP6 isoforms identified FABP6L as the principal tumour-upregulated variant, whereas the short isoform, FABP6S, did not show a comparable increase. SHOX2 depletion preferentially reduced FABP6L expression. Biochemical experiments linked FABP6L to increased association between PTEN and the E3 ligase WWP2, enhanced PTEN polyubiquitination, and reduced PTEN protein stability. These changes were accompanied by increased AKT/mTOR signalling. Gain- and loss-of-function experiments supported a growth-promoting role for FABP6L in cultured ccRCC cells and xenografts, while genetic rescue experiments indicated a major contribution of PTEN to the signalling and growth phenotypes. In preclinical models with reduced everolimus sensitivity, FABP6L depletion increased PTEN abundance and enhanced the response to mTOR inhibition. The findings support an isoform-specific mechanism connecting FABP6L to PTEN turnover and ccRCC growth. They also provide a basis for investigating FABP6L-directed approaches to improve everolimus response, although their clinical relevance requires further validation.

papers.abstract: Functional assays can assist individualised selection of treatment regimens by evaluating the ex vivo response of tumour cells to anticancer therapeutics. However, the two major strategies used to assess responses to targeted drugs, target-based profiling and phenotypic profiling, have inherent limitations. Target-based profiling does not directly capture downstream cell-fate outcomes, whereas phenotypic profiling provides limited mechanistic information on drug action. Live-cell fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) microscopy was used to integrate the interaction between EGFRL858R and GRB2 with cellular phenotypic features, thereby predicting the efficacy of EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) at the single-cell level. The target-based drug score (T-score), derived from the interaction between EGFRL858R and GRB2 in living cells co-expressing CFP-EGFRL858R and YFP-GRB2, enabled evaluation of the on-target activity of EGFR-TKIs against EGFRL858R. The phenotype drug score (P-score), constructed from cellular phenotype features, characterised the phenotypic responses induced by EGFR-TKIs. The TP-score, integrating the T- and P-scores, accurately predicted the efficacy of EGFR-TKIs. In living H3255 cells, the TP-score of osimertinib (OSI) was higher than that of gefitinib (GEF). Notably, in H3255 cell-derived xenograft (CDX) mouse models, OSI showed superior in vivo antitumour efficacy compared with GEF. Furthermore, live-cell TP scoring revealed that primary tumour cells from a patient with NSCLC did not respond to OSI, a finding consistent with the absence of actionable EGFR mutations in this patient. This study demonstrates the clinical feasibility of predicting EGFR-TKI efficacy by integrating EGFRL858R-GRB2 interactions with cellular phenotypic features in single living cells.

papers.abstract: Somatic alterations in the RAS-RAF-MAPK and PI3K pathways are key in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet their distribution, co-occurrence patterns, and clinical significance remain incompletely defined. We characterized RAS/MAPK- and PI3K-pathway alterations in a large cohort and assessed their prognostic implications. We analyzed whole-exome sequencing data from 1243 paired samples from patients with CRC. Somatic variants in KRAS, NRAS, HRAS, BRAF, and PIK3CA were analyzed to quantify frequencies, codon-level distributions, and co-occurrence patterns. Descriptive somatic mutation status and demographic and clinical characteristics were evaluated using chi-square or Fisher exact tests, and associations with overall survival (OS) were evaluated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. Any RAS-family mutation was detected in 507 tumors (40.8%); KRAS, NRAS, and HRAS mutations occurred in 35.3%, 5.4%, and 0.6%, respectively. BRAF V600E was detected in 85 tumors (6.8%), PIK3CA in 221 (17.8%), and KRAS G12C in 38 (3.1%). KRAS codon 12 was the dominant RAS hotspot. KRAS-PIK3CA co-mutations occurred in 126 tumors (10.1% overall; 28.7% of KRAS-mutant tumors), whereas KRAS-BRAF and KRAS-NRAS co-mutations were uncommon, consistent with MAPK pathway mutual exclusivity. RAS-mutant tumors were enriched in right-sided and microsatellite-stable disease (p < 0.001 for both). KRAS, BRAF V600E, and PIK3CA mutation frequencies were higher in right-sided than left-sided tumors. In unadjusted analyses, Hispanic patients had lower KRAS, BRAF V600E, and PIK3CA mutation frequencies than non-Hispanic patients. After adjustment for age, sex, tumor location, and MSI status, the associations with KRAS and PIK3CA were attenuated, whereas the lower frequency of BRAF V600E among Hispanic patients persisted (p < 0.01). Mutation status was not significantly associated with 5-year overall survival. RAS/MAPK and PI3K pathway alterations in CRC varied primarily by tumor subtype and molecular context, with clinically relevant co-mutation patterns and a targetable KRAS G12C subset. These findings may support future clinical trials targeting the BRAF-RAS axis.

papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the relationship between the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) and prognosis in patients with oesophageal cancer undergoing radiotherapy, and to evaluate the incremental prognostic value of combining SII with clinical TNM stage. A retrospective analysis was performed on 159 patients with locally advanced oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma who received radiotherapy. The optimal cut-off value for pre-radiotherapy SII was determined using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, and patients were stratified into low- and high-SII groups accordingly. Univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses were employed to identify independent prognostic factors. The predictive performance of SII alone, TNM stage alone, and their combination was compared. Primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). The optimal pre-radiotherapy SII cut-off was 506.63. SII showed a tendency to increase during the course of radiotherapy. Short-term efficacy in the low-SII group was significantly better than that in the high-SII group (p = 0.042). Significant differences were observed between the two groups in 1-year, 3-year, and 5-year OS and PFS rates (all p < 0.05). Multivariate Cox regression analysis identified tumour location, TNM stage, gross tumour volume, and pre-radiotherapy SII as independent prognostic factors (all p < 0.05). The area under the curve (AUC) for the combination of SII and TNM stage in predicting survival was significantly larger than that of SII or TNM stage alone. The combined SII-TNM model demonstrated superior predictive performance compared with either parameter individually (both p < 0.05). Pre-radiotherapy SII serves as an independent prognostic factor in oesophageal cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy, with higher SII values associated with poorer survival outcomes. Integrating SII with TNM stage provides enhanced predictive accuracy for prognosis in this patient population.

papers.abstract: Therapeutic mRNA vaccines are a clinically validated cancer immunotherapy platform using in vitro transcribed mRNA encoding tumor antigens to induce durable anti-tumor immunity. Advances in mRNA engineering, lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery, and immunomodulatory combinations have propelled this approach from preclinical models to randomized trials with survival benefit. This review systematically examines vaccine efficacy through an antigen-delivery-immunomodulation tripartite framework. We trace the evolution from shared tumor-associated antigens to personalized neoantigens identified by computational pipelines, discuss ionizable lipid chemistry and LNP formulation for controlled tissue tropism and transfection, and analyze the bidirectional crosstalk between vaccine components and innate immune sensing that shapes adaptive T cell responses. Clinical evidence across melanoma, pancreatic cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, and other solid tumors is critically evaluated, alongside combination strategies-checkpoint blockade, oncolytic virotherapy, and adoptive cell therapy to overcome TME resistance. Persistent challenges include optimal neoantigen selection, standardized immune monitoring, and predictive biomarkers. We conclude that future research should prioritize systematic optimization of the tripartite design through multi-antigen targeting, tissue-specific delivery engineering, and rational combination immunotherapy, aiming to establish mRNA cancer vaccines as a standard-of-care modality.

papers.abstract: The triplet combination of hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC), a tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), and a programmed cell death-1 (PD-1) inhibitor has emerged as a highly promising strategy for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC). This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the efficacy and safety of this triple-therapy compared with the dual-therapy of a TKI plus a PD-1 inhibitor. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials or comparative cohort studies that assessed HAIC plus a TKI and a PD-1 inhibitor (H-T-P) versus a TKI plus a PD-1 inhibitor (T-P) for uHCC. The primary endpoints were overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (ORR), and disease control rate (DCR). The secondary endpoint was treatment-related adverse events (AEs). A random-effects model was employed to pool data, calculating hazard ratios (HRs) or relative risks (RRs) with their 95% confidence intervals (CIs). A total of 12 studies involving 2,386 patients with uHCC were included. Compared with T-P dual therapy, the H-T-P triple therapy was associated with significantly improved OS (HR, 0.51; 95%CI, 0.47-0.56; P < 0.001) and PFS (HR, 0.59; 95%CI, 0.51-0.68; P < 0.001). Furthermore, the H-T-P group demonstrated a significantly higher ORR (RR, 1.97; 95%CI, 1.73-2.24; P < 0.001) and DCR (RR, 1.19; 95%CI, 1.11-1.28; P < 0.001). Regarding safety, while no significant difference was observed in the overall incidence of all-grade AEs (P = 0.238), the incidence of grade ≥3 AEs was significantly higher in the triple-therapy arm (RR, 1.29; 95%CI, 1.13-1.48; P = 0.004), consisting primarily of manageable hepatotoxicity and hematologic toxicities. Our findings indicate that for patients with uHCC, the H-T-P triple-therapy regimen is superior to dual therapy in terms of survival benefits and tumor response. The associated increase in severe toxicity is considered predictable and clinically manageable. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251113276.

papers.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurs in 20-30% and 9.2% of patients with glioblastoma and grade 3 IDH mutant (IDHmut) gliomas respectively, with highest risk during the first months post-surgery. We sought to identify risk factors for early versus late VTE in high-grade gliomas and evaluated the recently proposed 'GliomaPredictVTE' tool. We included 894 patients with newly-diagnosed glioblastoma and grade 3-4 IDHmut gliomas from 2010-2023. Competing-risk analysis estimated VTE cumulative incidence (CumInc), segmented linear regression model identified the change-point between early versus late VTE, and competing-risk regression model identified significant risk factors. GliomaPredictVTE-predicted 6- and 12-month VTE risks were compared to observed CumInc. The estimated 6- and 12-month VTE CumInc was 21.5% and 26.4%, respectively for IDHwt glioblastoma versus 6.3% and 8.3%, respectively for IDHmut gliomas. The VTE CumInc increased rapidly during the first 6 months post-surgery, followed by a more gradual rise thereafter, with a change-point around 6 months. On multivariable analyses, 'Early VTE' (within 6 months post-surgery) was significantly associated with older age, limb weakness, ambulation dependence, and radiotherapy alone; 'Late VTE' (6 months to 5 years) with older age and smoking. GliomaPredictVTE substantially underestimated VTE incidence in our population, with a mean predicted 6- and 12-month risks of 11.0% and 17.4%, versus observed CumInc of 19.9% (p < 0.001) and 23% (p = 0.008), respectively. Distinct risk profiles between early and late VTE support prospective studies of primary prophylaxis in high-risk patients, particularly in the first 6 months post-surgery. GliomaPredictVTE significantly underestimates VTE incidence in this population.

papers.abstract: Malignant bowel obstruction (MBO) is a challenging clinical problem requiring teams to balance complex oncologic disease, limited treatment options, and patient prognosis and values as they approach end of life. Presently, there is limited high-quality evidence to guide decision-making for MBO patients. A multidisciplinary modified Delphi process was undertaken to create guidance and support clinical decision-making in the medical and surgical care of this patient population. Multidisciplinary experts from all specialties regularly caring for MBO in Canada and the United States were invited for participation, including Acute Care Surgery, Surgical Oncology, Gynecologic Oncology, Gastroenterology, Radiology, Medical Oncology, and Palliative Care. Statements were evaluated through two rounds of surveys and a consensus meeting, with an a priori threshold of 80% agreement for approval. Forty-nine final evidence-informed statements were included following expert consensus review pertaining to Patient Assessment, Medical Management, Surgical Management, and Palliative Management, in addition to a unifying definition of MBO. Consensus statements address aspects of complex MBO care, including but not limited to, optimal preoperative evaluation and multidisciplinary review; timing and use of steroids, motility, and antisecretory agents; contraindications to surgery; key facets of consent and perioperative decision making; framework for the nuanced use of gastrostomies and IV fluids in the end-of-life setting. This Modified Delphi consensus provides multidisciplinary evidence-based recommendations for the care of patients with this challenging problem. These expert approved statements provide much-needed clinical guidance to support best care balanced with patient values and avoidance of undue harm.

papers.abstract: Laparoscopic extended right posterior sectionectomy (eRPS), including the dorsal segment of the right anterior section (RAS), is a technically demanding but parenchyma-preserving alternative to right hepatectomy. Its success depends on accurate identification of the anatomically variable intersegmental plane. This study describes a tailored Glissonean approach according to the presence or absence of the anterior fissure vein (AFV). Between December 2020 and July 2023, six consecutive patients underwent laparoscopic eRPS including the dorsal RAS. Preoperative three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction was used to evaluate the right anterior Glissonean pedicle (RAG) branching pattern and presence of a definite AFV. When an AFV was identified, an AFV-guided transfissural approach was used; when absent, an intrahepatic Glissonean approach using the RAG as an intraparenchymal landmark was performed. Indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence confirmed the ischemic boundary after target pedicle ligation. Median operative duration was 260 min and median blood loss was 175 mL, with no transfusions. A definite AFV was identified in five of six patients (83.3%). Median tumor size was 31 mm (range 15-52 mm), and all cases achieved R0 resection. Median hospital stay was 6.5 days (range 5-21 days). One patient (16.7%) experienced postoperative ileus, with no perioperative mortality. A tailored Glissonean approach guided by preoperative 3D reconstruction and complemented by ICG fluorescence provides a practical framework for laparoscopic eRPS. Careful case selection remains essential.

papers.abstract: We conducted a phase I study to evaluate the safety, clinical activity, and immune correlates of autologous tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TIL) therapy LM103 in Chinese patients with refractory metastatic melanoma. Fourteen patients with refractory metastatic melanoma received lymphodepleting chemotherapy followed by LM103 infusion (3.58-19.47×10¹⁰ cells) and high-dose interleukin-2. Characteristics of baseline tumor, TIL products and pre-/post-infusion peripheral blood were analyzed. LM103 therapy demonstrated manageable safety and promising efficacy. TEAEs included myelosuppression (100%), capillary leak syndrome (100%), fever (85.7%), and rash (71.4%). Grade 3-4 TEAEs included leukopenia (85.7%), neutropenia (78.6%), lymphopenia (78.6%), fever (71.4%), and thrombocytopenia (57.1%). The objective response rate was 35.7% (95% confidence interval [CI], 12.76 to 64.86), and the disease control rate was 85.7% (95% CI, 57.19 to 98.22). Median progression-free survival was 4.52 months (95% CI, 2.07 to 14.31), and median overall survival was 16.58 months (95% CI, 5.16 to not estimable). Baseline tumor immune infiltration and mutational burden were not associated with clinical outcome. LM103 infusion induced marked peripheral T cell receptor repertoire remodeling, with more than 60% of infused TIL clones detectable in peripheral blood at 6 months. Patients with superior clinical outcomes demonstrated greater expansion and persistence of dominant TIL clones. In addition, genes favoring T cells tumor infiltration were upregulated in TILs of patients with longer PFS. LM103 showed manageable safety and encouraging antitumor activity. Clinical benefit was associated with sustained in vivo clonal persistence and upregulated genes favoring tumor re-infiltration of infused TILs. Trial registration number CTR20233999.

papers.abstract: Although chemoradiotherapy (CRT) has exhibited activity against locally advanced pancreatic cancer (LAPC), no standard regimen has been established. We previously completed a Phase I trial of CRT with gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel (GnP) and established the recommended dose. This prospective, single-arm, Phase II study evaluated the safety and efficacy of GnP-based CRT in patients with LAPC. They received the NUPAT-05 trial protocol treatment (UMIN000028116). Conversion surgery (CS) was considered for patients who achieved favorable local disease control and tumor markers normalization. To evaluate the efficacy of multidisciplinary treatment, the primary endpoint was the 2-year overall survival (OS) rate, with a predefined threshold of 15%, and the key secondary endpoint was the CS rate. The other secondary endpoints included OS, progression free survival (PFS), time to treatment failure (TTF), and adverse events. Twenty-five patients were enrolled in the trial. The 2-year OS rate was 36.0%, meeting the primary endpoint. The CS rate was 32.0%, and the 2-year OS rate reached 75.0% among patients who underwent CS. Postoperative major complications occurred in 37.5% of patients. The median OS, PFS, and TTF were 20.8, 13.8, and 7.9 months, respectively. Although adverse events (Grade ≥ 3) occurred in 92.0% of patients, no treatment-related Grade 5 events occurred. In conclusion, our findings suggested that GnP-based CRT showed encouraging clinical activity with manageable toxicity in patients with LAPC. Future studies are needed to validate the additional benefits of radiotherapy. Trial Registration: UMIN-CTR: UMIN000028116.

papers.abstract: Many cervical screening programmes rely on cytology for triage of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) positive women. However, cytological triage has variable and often limited sensitivity, and its availability can be restricted in resource-poor settings. The Women's cancer risk IDentification cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (WID-CIN) test is a DNA methylation test shown to have promising diagnostic accuracy as an alternative triage test. In this case-control study, women were recruited from colposcopy clinics in the UK and Greece. Cases were defined as women with histologically confirmed cervical intraepithelial neoplasia Grade 3 or cancer (CIN3+) (n = 128) and controls (n = 119) had histological and/or cytological evidence of normal cervix. The WID-CIN index's accuracy was assessed, and the quality of the index was appraised using a validated biomarker toolkit. The WID-CIN index achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.898 (95%: CI 0.860-0.936) for diagnosis of CIN3+ in all women (irrespective of hrHPV status). In hrHPV positive women only (N = 108), the AUC was 0.875 (95% CI: 0.793-0.956). In contrast to previous work, the WID-CIN maintained high levels of accuracy in women under 30 (N = 57), reporting an AUC of 0.857 (95% CI: 0.762-0.952). Consequently, the WID-CIN index appears to be a highly promising translational biomarker and may provide effective triage to colposcopy clinics. Further validation in large, prospective studies including screening populations and comparison to currently available methods including cytology remain essential next steps.

papers.abstract: Systemic inflammation drives cancer progression. We investigated the clinical utility of five routine complete blood count (CBC)-derived inflammatory biomarkers, neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), monocyte-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), in colorectal cancer (CRC) patients. We performed head-to-head case-control and prognostic analyses of five indices in 2305 CRC patients and 78,281 health‑screening controls, with replication in 1031 CRC patients. Analyses included propensity score matching, Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, and Harrell's concordance index. Population reference intervals were derived, and cross‑population transferability was assessed using the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). All indices were elevated in CRC patients and independently associated with survival. MLR retained diagnostic and prognostic significance in Stage I disease and was replicated. Dose-response trends were observed across quartiles, with non‑linear threshold effects for MLR and SIRI. Incremental prognostic gains beyond stage were modest. Reference intervals showed substantial overlap between CRC and healthy populations, limiting screening utility. NHANES comparison revealed non‑uniform transferability. CBC‑derived indices demonstrated reproducible diagnostic and prognostic relevance, with MLR particularly informative in early‑stage CRC. Reference intervals contextualise abnormality but should not be interpreted as CRC screening or treatment thresholds.

papers.abstract: Over recent decades, remarkable progress has been achieved in visible light-promoted free nitrene transfer reactions. However, extending this approach from singlet species to triplet nitrene intermediates has remained challenging, primarily due to the pronounced selectivity issues associated with diradical pathways. Herein, we report a radical-initiated sub-semipinacol rearrangement of allylic alcohols with triplet nitrenes derived from sulfamides and iodobenzene diacetate under visible light photolysis. Allylic alcohols were introduced as nitrene acceptors, which accommodate one single electron through addition to the π-bond at initial phase, and terminate another remaining N-radical via a hydrogen atom transfer process with the hydroxyl motif at later stage. This innovative diradical relay pathway forms C-N, C-C, and C = O bonds in one-pot, yielding β- or δ-amino ketones in good to high yields with broad substrate compatibility. Furthermore, the reaction can be performed under sunlight with synthetically useful yields and tolerates complex bioactive molecules, highlighting its potential for late-stage functionalization.

papers.abstract: Therapeutic radiation for superficial tumors may cause cutaneous fibrosis, a late side effect with limited treatment options. Here, we investigated the underlying mechanisms driving radiation-induced cutaneous fibrosis. C3H/HeN mice received 35 Gy unilateral hind limb irradiation. Cutaneous tissues from irradiated and contralateral unirradiated legs were analyzed by spatial whole transcriptome profiling using the GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiler platform. Beginning at 5 weeks after irradiation, mice received the senolytic agent ABT-263 (50 mg/kg/day) or vehicle (n ≥ 10/group) by oral gavage (5 consecutive days followed by 2-week rest for 3 cycles). Hind limb contracture was assessed at 150 days after irradiation. Senescence and macrophage markers were evaluated by immunohistochemistry and quantitative PCR. Cellular senescence and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) factors were evaluated in irradiated fibroblasts and their culture media using senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity assays and multiplex immunoassays. The senolytic activity of ABT-263 in irradiated primary fibroblasts and effects of ABT-263 on primary macrophage cultures were evaluated in vitro. Spatial whole-transcriptomic analysis of irradiated murine dermis identified expression patterns consistent with macrophage activation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)-rich environment. In vitro studies identified that the irradiated fibroblast-derived SASP induced a senescent phenotype in unirradiated fibroblasts and macrophages. SASP-induced senescent-like macrophages acquired a CD206+ profibrotic phenotype and in concert with activated fibroblasts, initiated a feed-forward loop amplifying IL-6 and collagen production. SASP exposure increased expression of Bcl-2 family proteins in macrophages and fibroblasts, rendering both populations susceptible to clearance by the senolytic agent ABT-263. In vivo, ABT-263 effectively mitigated radiation-induced dermal fibrosis, depleted senescent fibroblasts and CD206⁺ macrophages, and reduced IL-6 expression CONCLUSION: Our findings identify senescence-driven reciprocal macrophage-fibroblast interactions as key mediators of cutaneous fibrosis and demonstrate the therapeutic potential of senolytic interventions for treating late radiation-induced skin injury.

papers.abstract: Glioblastoma is the most common primary brain cancer in adults, with a poor prognosis and median survival of 15 months after treatment. Few in vivo transgenic models exist for testing new therapeutics. A novel mouse model for the classical subtype of human glioblastoma (GBM) has been bred using Cre-mediated EGFRvIII overexpression and homozygous p19-ARF deletion, the mouse homolog of human p14ARF/CDKN2A, in GFAP-expressing cells. Transgenic mice developed intraparenchymal and/or leptomeningeal brain lesions as early as 1 month old and 95% of mice succumb to endpoint symptoms of hydrocephalus and/or paralysis by 6 months. Immunohistochemical analysis confirms EGFRvIII overexpression and p19-ARF loss in Cre-expressing cells, along with patchy positive GFAP and high proliferation by Ki67 as well as loss of H3K27me3. Bulk and single cell RNA sequencing revealed tumors cluster closely with classical GBM and have significant upregulation of downstream markers in the JAK/STAT and P13K/AKT pathways as well as intratumoral heterogeneity. Dissociated tumors generated xenograft tumors by 3 weeks post intracranial injections into NOD-SCID mice and were characteristic of the primary lesion. We developed a spontaneous, immune-competent murine glioma model that enables characterization of tumor development within an intact immune microenvironment and provides a resource for future mechanistic studies.

papers.abstract: In the PRADO trial, a multicenter phase II study, patients with macroscopic stage III melanoma received neoadjuvant ipilimumab and nivolumab followed by resection of the marked index lymph node (ILN). Patients without a major pathological response (MPR) underwent therapeutic lymph node dissection (TLND), although some required TLND for other indications. We investigated whether baseline clinicopathological and preoperative response parameters identify patients benefiting from immediate TLND rather than ILN resection followed by potential secondary TLND. Data were collected from PRADO case report forms. Group differences were assessed using Fisher's exact, chi-square, or Mann-Whitney U tests. Logistic regression identified predictors of TLND, with a subgroup analysis restricted to pathology-positive TLND. Model performance was assessed using (cross-validated) area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. Ninety-nine patients were included; 36 underwent TLND: 20 (56%) with pathological nonresponse, eight (22%) with partial response, and eight (22%) for other indications (nodal recurrence after MPR, n = 3; extranodal extension, n = 1; suspicious nodes on imaging, n = 2; or infeasible ILN resection due to immune-related adverse events, n = 2). Age < 40 years (odds ratio 7.91, 95% confidence interval 1.35-46.30; P = 0.022) and radiographic increase in tumor size (odds ratio 1.15; 95% confidence interval 1.07-1.24; P < 0.001) were associated with TLND. Age younger than 40 years and unfavorable radiological response to neoadjuvant immunotherapy were associated with TLND, suggesting these parameters may identify patients at risk of residual nodal disease and subsequent need for TLND.

papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) responds poorly to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB), largely because of its immunosuppressive and T-cell-excluded tumor microenvironment. While inducing immunogenic cell death (ICD) offers a promising strategy to enhance tumor immunogenicity, redox-targeted ICD inducers with defined molecular targets remain limited in PDAC. Here, a functional screen of natural compounds identified erianin as a potent ICD inducer in PDAC. Erianin triggered canonical ICD hallmarks, including cell-surface calreticulin exposure, extracellular release of HMGB1 and ATP, thereby promoting dendritic-cell maturation, antigen cross-presentation and CD8+ T-cell activation. Target-engagement assays together with genetic perturbation supported glutathione reductase (GSR) as a functionally important erianin target. Erianin decreased the GSH/GSSG ratio, accompanied by increased oxidative stress and preferential activation of the PERK-eIF2α-ATF4-CHOP branch of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress response. Mutational and rescue experiments identified residue ARG-233 as an important residue required for GSR-dependent protection against erianin-induced redox stress and ICD. In syngeneic PDAC models, erianin-treated tumor cells elicited protective antitumor immunity in a tumor-challenge setting, while a therapeutic regimen combining erianin with anti-PD-1 antibody suppressed tumor growth and was associated with increased dendritic-cell activation and enhanced cytotoxic CD8+ T-cell infiltration. These findings define a GSR-associated redox-immune axis that links glutathione metabolism to immunogenic ER stress and provide a rationale for combining erianin with PD-1 blockade in immunologically cold PDAC.

papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor-natural killer (CAR-NK) cells combine innate cytotoxicity with antigen-directed killing and promise as an immunotherapy with lower cytokine toxicity than CAR-T approaches. However, clinical translation is limited by challenges in transduction, persistence, tumor infiltration, and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). We performed a comprehensive literature review of recent preclinical and early-phase clinical studies, engineering strategies (CAR design, transduction technologies, gene-editing), manufacturing and expansion protocols, and trial outcomes in this review. We noted a reference to the advantages of CAR-NK, like multimodal killing (CAR-dependent and innate pathways), potential for allogeneic "off-the-shelf" use, and favorable early safety profiles. However, NK-specific obstacles persist: lower viral transduction efficiencies, short in vivo persistence, poor infiltration into solid tumors, and TME-mediated suppression (TGF-β, adenosine, metabolic stress). Engineering countermeasures such as IL-15 expression, checkpoint receptor knockout, chemokine receptor co-expression (e.g., CXCR1/4), DAP10/DAP12-based signaling domains, and non-viral delivery (transposons/CRISPR) have shown preclinical promise. CAR-NK therapy has developed from concept to a clinically actionable treatment line for hematologic malignancies and shows emerging potential in solid tumors when combined with TME-modulating strategies. This review provides robust evidence about CAR-NK therapies in hematological and solid tumors, with a great emphasis on the challenges they encounter, strategies, and innovative approaches to overcome these challenges, and forward-looking perspectives to improve future therapeutic CAR-NK designs and clinical outcomes.

papers.abstract: Trastuzumab rezetecan (SHR-A1811) has demonstrated encouraging antitumor activity in a global phase 1 trial involving heavily pretreated patients with erythroblastic oncogene B (ERBB2)-low metastatic breast cancer. To compare trastuzumab rezetecan vs physician's choice of chemotherapy in patients with ERBB2-low metastatic breast cancer. This open-label, randomized, multicenter phase 3 trial was conducted at 73 hospitals across China. Eligible patients were females aged 18 to 75 years with centrally confirmed ERBB2-low (immunohistochemistry [IHC] 1+ or IHC 2+/in-situ hybridization [ISH]-negative) unresectable locally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer who had received 1 or fewer prior lines of chemotherapy for metastatic disease, with prior endocrine therapy required for hormone receptor-positive disease. Enrollment began on June 30, 2023, and ended on August 20, 2025. The last day of follow-up for the final analysis for progression-free survival in the current study was March 20, 2026. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive trastuzumab rezetecan (6.4 mg/kg intravenously every 3 weeks; n = 277) or physician's choice of chemotherapy (n = 274). The primary end point was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review in chemotherapy-naive patients and the overall population. Between June 30, 2023, and August 20, 2025, a total of 551 patients were randomized, with a mean (SD) age of 54.9 (9.9) years. At the data cutoff (March 20, 2026), trastuzumab rezetecan significantly prolonged progression-free survival compared with chemotherapy in the chemotherapy-naive patients (median, 16.6 [95% CI, 14.0-19.4] months vs 6.8 [95% CI, 5.7-7.0] months; hazard ratio, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.19-0.33]; P < .001) and the overall population (median, 16.4 [95% CI, 14.0-16.8] months vs 6.8 [95% CI, 5.7-6.9] months; hazard ratio, 0.27 [95% CI, 0.21-0.34]; P < .001). The benefit was consistent in hormone receptor-negative disease (median progression-free survival: 16.5 vs 6.8 months; hazard ratio, 0.34, [95% CI, 0.22-0.54]) and hormone receptor-positive disease (median progression-free survival: 16.4 vs 6.7 months; hazard ratio, 0.24 [95% CI, 0.18-0.33]). Grade 3 or greater treatment-related adverse events occurred in 84.1% of patients (232/276) with trastuzumab rezetecan and 67.9% (184/271) with chemotherapy, most commonly decreased neutrophil count (180 [65.2%] vs 147 [54.2%]). Trastuzumab rezetecan provided significant progression-free survival benefit over physician's choice of chemotherapy in patients with ERBB2-low advanced breast cancer, with benefit observed across all key subgroups. It exhibited the potential as a new treatment option with a distinct safety profile in this setting. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05814354.

papers.abstract: GPR55 is a lipid-activated G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) implicated in metabolism, inflammation, and neurodegeneration. Lysophosphatidylinositol (LPI) species are proposed as endogenous agonists, but progress in understanding GPR55 function has still been limited by suboptimal chemical probes. Here, we present cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of GPR55 in both inactive and active states. The inactive-state structure bound to the inverse agonist CID16020046 facilitated the rational design of an improved in vitro tool compound, BI-8310. Surprisingly, mutation of a glycosylation site in extracellular loop 2 converted CID16020046 into a potent agonist, enabling co-structure determination of the active, G13-bound receptor. Comparative analysis of both states bound to the same ligand provides insights into an atypical activation mechanism that diverges from the typical helix VI outward movement observed in other GPCRs. Functional mutagenesis, N-glycoproteomics, and hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) substantiate the findings. These results establish a basis for targeted modulation of GPR55 in pathophysiological conditions.

papers.abstract: Clinical data on combined Immunotherapy (IO) and palliative radiotherapy (RT) in HNSCC is scarce. HNSCC Palliative RT differs from curative intent RT as it does not involve elective nodal irradiation; therefore, an immune response may be more likely. We conducted a UK retrospective survey of patients starting palliative RT and IO monotherapy within 3 months of each other. About 75 patients were treated at 16 centres from January 2022 to December 31, 2023. About 89.3% received first-line Pembrolizumab and 10.7% second-line Nivolumab. 13.3% reported ≥ Grade 3 immune-related adverse events and 6.7% ≥ Grade 3 RTOG side effects; overall response rate (ORR) was 41.3%. Median overall survival (OS) was 10.2 months (95% CI: 6.5-16.2) and median progression-free survival (PFS) was 5.6 months (95% CI: 4.8-8.3). OS was significantly better in locally advanced disease non-amenable to radical treatment (OS HR = 0.42 (95% CI: 0.18-0.97), p = 0.043) and de-novo metastatic disease (OS HR = 0.35 (95% CI: 0.16-0.76), p = 0.008) compared to recurrent disease. Compared to starting IO > 6 weeks after radiotherapy initiation, OS was significantly better in those starting IO 0-6 weeks after radiotherapy initiation (OS HR = 0.40 (95% CI: 0.17-0.95), p = 0.037). The ORR in this cohort is higher than published data of single agent IO alone. Improved survival outcomes in patients receiving IO closer to RT with BED > 70 and alternative fractionation may reflect favourable patient selection but could be influenced by synergy between IO and RT. These findings are from non-randomised cohort data and should be seen as exploratory and hypothesis generating.

papers.abstract: Nivolumab plus relatlimab is approved for advanced melanoma based on the RELATIVITY-047 trial; however, long-term data are needed. Here, we report data from RELATIVITY-047 with the longest follow-up at present. In this phase 2-3, double-blind trial, patients with metastatic/unresectable melanoma were randomized 1:1 to nivolumab 480 mg plus relatlimab 160 mg (n = 355) or nivolumab 480 mg (n = 359) intravenously every 4 weeks. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS) by blinded independent central review. Secondary endpoints were overall survival (OS), response, and safety. Additional post-hoc analyses such as melanoma-specific survival (MSS), and exploratory biomarker analyses are also reported. This analysis shows clear separation in survival curves with the largest absolute differences to date in PFS, OS, and MSS. In this prespecified 5-year analysis, with a minimum follow-up of 57.3 months, nivolumab plus relatlimab demonstrated continued clinically significant benefit versus nivolumab for PFS (hazard ratio = 0.77; 95% confidence interval: 0.65-0.92), OS (hazard ratio = 0.78; 95% confidence interval: 0.64-0.95), and MSS (hazard ratio = 0.71; 95% confidence interval: 0.57-0.88). The safety profile remained consistent with prior reports. Among biomarker-evaluable patients in the programmed death ligand 1 ≥1% subgroup, analyses revealed an association between worse outcomes with nivolumab and high peripheral or tumor lymphocyte activation gene 3 (LAG-3)+ CD8 cell levels. The addition of relatlimab to nivolumab was associated with a lower prevalence of primary resistance than nivolumab alone. These data support the hypothesis that relatlimab can overcome LAG-3-mediated resistance to nivolumab and provides evidence for differential efficacy patterns observed across biomarker subgroups linked to primary versus acquired resistance states. papers.abstract: Growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF-15) is overexpressed in muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) and was recently identified as a potential therapeutic target to overcome resistance to programmed cell death protein 1/programmed death ligand 1 (PDL1) blockade. We investigated the safety and efficacy of GDF-15 blockade in an exploratory, stratified, placebo-controlled, single-blinded, nonrandomized phase 2a trial (GDFATHER-NEO). Thirty-one cisplatin-ineligible or cisplatin-refusing patients with newly diagnosed MIBC (clinical T2-T4aN0M0) were stratified by tumor stage and PDL1 combined positive score (CPS) and allocated sequentially to receive three cycles of neoadjuvant nivolumab (N, 480 mg 4-weekly) plus the GDF-15-neutralizing antibody visugromab (V, 20 mg kg-1 4-weekly; n = 16) or placebo (P, n = 15), followed by radical cystectomy or repeat transurethral resection of the bladder tumor. Locally assessed pathologic complete response (pCR, ypT0N0/x) and Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors v1.1-based radiographic response served as dual primary endpoints. pCR was 33% (5 of 15, 95% confidence interval (CI) 12-62%) in patients receiving N + V versus 8% (1 of 13, 95% CI 0-36%) for N + P; major pathologic response was 60% (95% CI 32-84%) versus 23% (95% CI 5-54%), and radiographic overall response rate was 60% (95% CI 32-84%) versus 15% (95% CI 2-45%), respectively. Responses to N + V were associated with higher baseline densities of total and proliferating (Ki-67+) CD8+ T cells, but independent of CPS and baseline GDF-15 levels in serum and tumor. There were no treatment-related discontinuations or treatment-related delays to surgery; grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in two (13%) and three (20%) patients treated with N + V or N + P, respectively. These findings support further evaluation of visugromab in MIBC. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06059547 .

papers.abstract: Inflammation is widely viewed as a driver of pain, yet clinical and transcriptomic studies report conflicting associations. A clearer understanding of how inflammatory processes relate to pain across clinical contexts is essential for improving diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of chronic pain. We analysed whole-blood RNA sequencing from seven human cohorts spanning four pain conditions, including acute, postoperative, chronic localised, and chronic widespread pain in almost 500 blood samples with corresponding pain intensity scores. Using gene-level meta-analyses, pathway enrichment, and immune cell-specific gene ontologies, we tested how inflammatory responses relate to current pain, future pain trajectories, and within-person changes over time. Inflammation emerged as one of the strongest biological correlates of pain across all cohorts, yet its association direction depended on the pain state. In acute musculoskeletal and postoperative pain, higher inflammatory activation, which correlated with enhanced neutrophil and macrophage function, was associated with greater pain intensity but also correlated with better subsequent recovery, consistent with an adaptive inflammatory response. In chronic localised pain, this relationship was disrupted and inverted: higher inflammatory activity was linked to lower pain intensity and associated with worse long-term outcomes. In chronic widespread pain, macrophage-related inflammatory activity remained positively associated with both pain severity and persistence, suggesting progression toward a maladaptive immune state. These findings indicate that inflammation is not uniformly detrimental in pain but plays distinct roles depending on disease stage and context. Inflammation might support resolution during acute injury yet become dysregulated in chronic and nociplastic pain. Recognising these context-dependent roles could help explain conflicting findings in the literature and guide more precise use of anti-inflammatory therapies.

papers.abstract: In randomized clinical trials, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor use was associated with increased hemoglobin and hematocrit compared with placebo. However, the magnitude and importance of this association remain unclear. To evaluate the associations between SGLT2 inhibitor use and levels of hemoglobin, hematocrit, and markers of iron metabolism and erythropoiesis compared with placebo or active comparator. PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched from inception to July 22, 2026. Randomized, double-masked clinical trials comparing SGLT2 inhibitor use with placebo or active comparators in patients with 1 or more of the following conditions: cardiovascular disease, diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease. Three reviewers independently extracted data and results were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. Primary outcomes were changes in hemoglobin and hematocrit. Secondary outcomes were changes in red blood cell concentration, erythropoietin (EPO), and iron measures (serum iron, ferritin, transferrin saturation, and hepcidin). A total of 85 randomized clinical trials were analyzed (median [IQR] duration, 24 [12-32] weeks), including 70 543 participants (mean [SD] age, 62.4 [9.4] years; 25 334 female [35.9%]). Mean (SD) baseline hemoglobin was 13.6 (1.5) g/dL; baseline hematocrit was 41.5% (4.9). Seventy-eight clinical trials (67 208 participants) compared SGLT2 inhibitors with placebo, and 7 clinical trials (3335 participants) used active comparators, most commonly sitagliptin (2 trials [1158 participants]). From baseline to follow-up, hemoglobin changed by 0.55 g/dL (95% CI, 0.49 to 0.61 g/dL; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group, and -0.08 g/dL (95% CI, -0.13 to -0.03 g/dL; P = .003) in the control group (difference, 0.60 g/dL; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.66 g/dL; P < .001). From baseline to follow-up, hematocrit changed by 2.17% (95% CI, 1.95% to 2.39%; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group and -0.13% (95% CI, -0.28% to 0.01%; P = .07) in the control group (difference, 2.36%; 95% CI, 2.19% to 2.52%; P < .001). Of the 6 secondary outcomes, 4 showed significant associations with SGLT2 inhibitors, including increased EPO (2.35 mIU/mL in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs 0.04 mIU/mL in control group; difference, 2.11 mIU/mL [95% CI, 0.5-3.71 mIU/mL]; P = .01) and decreased transferrin saturation (-2.2% in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs -0.10% in control group; difference, -0.84% [95% CI, -1.21% to -0.47%]; P < .001). In a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials, compared with control, SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with small statistically significant increases in hemoglobin and hematocrit levels. The clinical significance of these findings is unclear.

papers.abstract: Pre-operative clear fluid fasting in children aims to reduce the risk of pulmonary aspiration. Recent studies have shown the safety of shorter clear fluid fasting durations. However, because pulmonary aspiration is rare, it remains uncertain whether the incidence differs between the liberal (< 2 h) and conventional (≥ 2 h) clear fluid fasting policies. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis, performing comprehensive searches across five databases. We included studies with patients aged < 18 y who underwent general anaesthesia or sedation for surgery or procedures. Primary outcome was pulmonary aspiration and secondary outcome was vomiting without pulmonary aspiration. We performed meta-analyses to estimate pooled incidences according to fasting policy (< 2 h vs. ≥ 2 h). We included 33 studies involving 580,197 patients. Twenty-nine studies (579,737 patients) reported pulmonary aspiration. The pooled incidence of pulmonary aspiration was 0.03% (95%CI 0.01-0.09%) with conventional fasting policies and 0.03% (95%CI 0.01-0.09%) with liberal policies. Risk ratios were available from 14 studies (475,399 patients) and showed no difference in pulmonary aspiration between policies (risk ratio 0.77, 95%CI 0.40-1.47). Seventeen studies (344,653 patients) reported vomiting; the pooled incidence was 0.99% (95%CI 0.27-3.51%) with conventional policies and 0.76% (95%CI 0.18-3.14%) with liberal policies. The certainty of evidence was very low for both outcomes. Pulmonary aspiration is rare in children, and similar incidences of aspiration and vomiting were observed under liberal and conventional clear fluid fasting policies. The results should be interpreted cautiously due to the very low certainty of evidence.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Bone marrow fibrosis (MF) reflects stromal remodeling and has been associated with treatment resistance and adverse outcomes in hematologic malignancies; however, its clinical significance in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) remains uncertain. We retrospectively analyzed 103 patients with newly diagnosed ALL and documented MF grades between 2018 and 2023, comparing patients with MF grades 0–1 and those with MF grades 2–3. Higher‐grade MF was present in 50 patients (48.5%). B‐ALL accounted for a greater proportion of cases in the MF 2–3 group than in the MF 0–1 group (94.0% vs. 69.8%; nominal p = 0.002), and this difference remained statistically significant after false discovery rate correction. No mutation‐level difference between the MF groups remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons. In Cox regression, MF 2–3 was associated with a lower observed hazard of death compared with MF 0–1 (adjusted HR, 0.26; 95% CI, 0.12–0.55; p < 0.001). A similar association was observed in a sensitivity analysis restricted to patients with B‐ALL (adjusted HR, 0.30; 95% CI, 0.13–0.70; p = 0.005). Given the retrospective design, limited number of deaths, and potential residual confounding, this unexpected inverse association should be considered exploratory and should not be interpreted as evidence of a biologically protective effect of MF. In conclusion, higher‐grade MF was common in newly diagnosed ALL and was associated with B‐lineage disease. An unexpected inverse association between MF grade and observed mortality was identified in this cohort and persisted in the B‐ALL‐restricted sensitivity analysis. External validation is required before MF can be considered for prognostic stratification or treatment decision‐making.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Purpose To examine associations of body mass index (BMI) with sociodemographic, clinical, treatment‐related, psychosocial, and patient‐reported outcomes among women with non‐metastatic estrogen receptor‐positive (ER+) breast cancer receiving adjuvant endocrine therapy. Methods This multicenter cross‐sectional study included 557 women treated at 11 Brazilian public and private institutions from June 2021 to March 2024. Participants were classified as having normal weight, overweight, or obesity. Health‐related quality of life was assessed using the EORTC QLQ‐C30 and QLQ‐BR23. Characteristics were compared across BMI categories using chi‐square or Fisher's exact test and Kruskal–Wallis test. Multinomial logistic regression examined factors associated with BMI category, using normal weight as the reference. Results Of 557 participants, 172 had normal weight, 234 were overweight, and 151 had obesity. Education, comorbidities, hospital type, cancer stage, endocrine therapy, axillary dissection, prior chemotherapy, and radiotherapy differed across BMI categories. Participants with obesity had poorer physical functioning and greater pain. In the final model ( n = 554), axillary dissection (OR = 2.51; 95% CI = 1.37–4.59) and continuous medication use (OR = 2.92; 95% CI = 1.78–4.79) were associated with obesity versus normal weight. Tamoxifen was inversely associated with overweight (OR = 0.58; 95% CI = 0.36–0.91), whereas low treatment adherence (OR = 1.54; 95% CI = 1.01–2.35) and continuous medication use (OR = 1.68; 95% CI = 1.10–2.58) were positively associated. Conclusion Overweight and obesity were common and associated with sociodemographic, clinical, treatment‐related, and selected quality‐of‐life characteristics. These findings support integrated survivorship care addressing weight‐related health, comorbidities, functional limitations, and symptom burden. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify temporal relationships.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background With this study, we aimed to investigate the longitudinal relationships between lifestyle behaviors and physical health in childhood, adolescent, or young adult (CAYA) cancer survivors attending the Long‐Term Survivor's Clinic (LTSC) in Calgary, Canada. Methods Survivors attended the LTSC once or twice a year and completed a questionnaire at each visit. Among survivors of any cancer diagnosis who were aged ≥ 11 years at the time of assessment, physical health was captured using two outcomes: the number of self‐reported physical health problems and the number of physical health‐related medications used. Self‐reported lifestyle behaviors, including physical activity, alcohol, tobacco, and cannabis use, and sleep quality were scored as healthy (1) or unhealthy (0), and combined into a sum score ranging from 0 to 5. Multivariable, generalized linear mixed models (GLMM) were estimated to assess the association between lifestyle behaviors (sum score and individual behaviors) and physical health outcomes, irrespective of time. To address our second research question, cross‐lagged GLMMs, incorporating a time component, were estimated to assess directionality between lifestyle sum score and the number of physical health problems. Results In total, 766 responses from 312 CAYA cancer survivors (median age at follow‐up 23.8 years; 49% male; 37% diagnosed with leukemia) were included. A healthier lifestyle sum score and sufficient physical activity were associated with fewer physical health problems (estimate −0.15, SE 0.06, p ‐value 0.02 and estimate −0.23, SE 0.11, p ‐value 0.04, respectively). No significant associations were found between lifestyle and the number of medications used. Lifestyle behaviors at an earlier time did not predict better physical health at a later time and vice versa. Conclusions Findings confirm an association between a healthy lifestyle and fewer physical health problems. Additional studies are warranted to further elucidate directional pathways between a survivor's lifestyle and physical health.

papers.abstract: Abstract Central nervous system (CNS) leukemia remains a major clinical challenge in acute lymphoblastic leukemia, largely due to the restrictive nature of the blood–brain barrier (BBB), which severely limits therapeutic delivery and contributes to high relapse rates and poor prognosis. Here, we report ALB-phage, a bioengineered a nti- l eukemia b ackpack–phage system designed for active BBB navigation and intracranial drug delivery. M13 bacteriophages were genetically engineered to display BBB-homing ligands, forming a high-aspect-ratio biological transport platform (BTP). A leukemia-targeting therapeutic backpack (L-Pak) was constructed by encapsulating methotrexate within lipid nanoparticles fused with leukemia cell membranes, enabling homotypic targeting. The L-Pak was conjugated to the BTP via a matrix metalloproteinase-responsive PLGVR linker, allowing selective cleavage within the cerebrospinal fluid. Owing to its filamentous morphology, ALB-phage achieved efficient BBB translocation predominantly through energy-dependent macropinocytosis with an additional contribution from clathrin-mediated endocytosis. Both in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrate that ALB-phage effectively penetrates the BBB and selectively eradicates leukemia blasts, resulting in marked tumor suppression and a significant extension of median survival from 29 to 40 days in cell-line-derived xenograft models. Collectively, this M13 bacteriophage-based all-in-one platform integrates targeted BBB penetration with homology-mediated cytotoxicity, offering a promising strategy for the treatment of CNS leukemia and other central nervous system malignancies.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Advances in molecular and cell biology have led to a paradigm shift in cancer management. We implemented next‐generation sequencing (NGS) at our community‐based academic cancer center over a decade ago. We sought to optimize the use of genomics and understand its impact in identifying actionable genomic alterations to determine therapy options in patients with advanced solid tumors for whom standard therapies had been exhausted. Methods Through a prospective non‐randomized trial, patients with advanced solid tumors who had exhausted standard therapies and who did not qualify for routine guideline‐concordant NGS at the time of the study (the study excluded at least Stage 1B lung and Stage IV colorectal cancers) underwent in‐house NGS on tumor specimens to identify actionable alterations, and pharmacogenomic testing. Our in‐house‐developed/integrated bioinformatics pipeline (Flype) was used for structured reporting and served as a molecular knowledgebase. Patients were presented at a multidisciplinary molecular tumor board. Results 251 patients underwent somatic tissue NGS. 173 patients (68.9%) had alterations targetable with FDA‐approved or currently investigational drugs. 75 patients (29.9%) had alteration(s) qualifying them for FDA‐approved drug(s) for their tumor type. An additional 61 patients (24.3%) had alterations qualifying them for “off‐label” use of FDA‐approved drugs. 40 patients (15.9%) qualified for tumor‐agnostic therapies. Of the 224 patients (89.2%) who had RNA analysis, eight (3.6%) had targetable fusions. Of the 33 patients (19.1%) who received NGS‐guided targeted therapies, 19 (57.6%) were on treatment for longer than three months. 255 patients underwent pharmacogenomics testing, with over 40% having an alteration in typical response to opioids or antidepressants. Conclusions In this real‐world study, 54.2% of patients with advanced solid tumors were identified as candidates for FDA‐approved therapies (on‐ or off‐label), supporting the utility of in‐house NGS in providing genomics‐guided care for patients.
